questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A popular food blogger from State A got into a heated online argument with the owner of a successful vegan restaurant located in State B about the merits of veganism. To get back at the owner, the blogger wrote a review of the owner's vegan restaurant in which she falsely claimed that the restaurant was infested with vermin and used animal products in its cuisine. The blogger had never eaten at the owner's restaurant or traveled to State B. The blog post had over 500,000 views from people around the United States. Within one month of the post, the restaurant shut down.
The owner sued the blogger in a federal court in State B for defamation. Based on the allegations in the owner's complaint, the blogger filed a motion to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction.
State B has a long-arm statute that gives its courts personal jurisdiction over out-of-state defendants that intentionally harm State B residents or businesses.
How will the federal court likely rule on the blogger's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the blogger knew that her review would negatively impact the restaurant in State B.
choices.B: Deny the motion, unless the blogger failed to attach an affidavit to the motion demonstrating why personal jurisdiction does not exist.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the blogger has never traveled to State B.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the blogger wrote the review in State A.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Requirements for specific jurisdiction
Long-arm
statute		 Forum state statute must authorize jurisdiction under specific circumstances
Due
process		 Minimum
contacts		 Purposeful availment of forum state's laws so suit is foreseeable:
  • Stream of commerce test – defendant places goods in stream of commerce & takes action that intentionally targets forum state
  • Effects test – defendant commits intentional tort in one state with intent that effects will be felt in forum state
Fair play &
substantial
justice		 Reasonableness factors:
  • Burden on defendant to appear & defend in forum state
  • Plaintiff's interest in obtaining relief in forum state
  • Forum state's interest
  • Interstate judicial system's interest in obtaining most efficient resolution of disputes
  • Interest of several states in furthering fundamental substantive social policies

A federal court* has specific personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant if (1) the forum state has a long-arm statute that authorizes jurisdiction under the specific circumstances and (2) applying that statute complies with due process. This due process requirement is met when:

  • the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and
  • the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

Minimum contacts exist when the defendant purposefully avails him/herself of the state's protections and benefits so that the defendant should reasonably foresee being sued there. Purposeful availment can occur even if the defendant never physically enters the forum state—eg, committing an intentional tort in one state with the intent that the effects will be felt in the forum state ((Choices C & D)).

(Choice A) Here, State B's long-arm statute authorizes jurisdiction over out-of-state defendants (the blogger) who intentionally harm a State B business or resident (the owner). Applying the statute complies with due process because the blogger purposefully availed herself of State B's benefits when she wrote a review to harm the owner in State B—making this defamation suit foreseeable there. And since there is no indication that exercising jurisdiction would offend notions of fair play and substantial justice, the State B federal court has specific jurisdiction over the blogger. Therefore, her motion to dismiss will likely be denied.

*Federal courts have the same jurisdictional reach as courts of the state in which they sit.

(Choice B) When a defendant asserts lack of personal jurisdiction in a pre-answer motion to dismiss (as seen here), the defendant can use the allegations in the pleadings or an attached affidavit to show why personal jurisdiction does not exist.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant has minimum contacts with a forum state when he/she purposefully avails him/herself of the state's protections and benefits, so that a lawsuit is reasonably foreseeable there. This can occur when the defendant commits an intentional tort in one state with the purpose or knowledge that the effects will be felt in the forum state.

📚 References
  • Calder v. Jones, 465 U.S. 783, 789–90 (1984) (holding that out-of-state defendants were subject to specific jurisdiction because their libelous article intentionally targeted the forum state's resident).
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the minimum contacts required for specific jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
一位来自A州的知名美食博主与一位位于B州的成功素食餐厅老板就素食主义的优点问题，在网上发生了激烈争吵。为了报复该老板，博主撰写了一篇关于该素食餐厅的评论，她在其中虚假声称该餐厅鼠虫滋生，并在其菜肴中使用动物产品。该博主从未在该老板的餐厅用餐，也从未去过B州。该博客文章获得了来自美国各地超过50万次的浏览量。发布该文章后一个月内，该餐厅倒闭了。
该老板在B州的联邦法院起诉该博主，指控其诽谤 (defamation)。根据老板诉状中的指控，博主提交了一份以缺乏人身管辖权 (personal jurisdiction) 为由的驳回动议 (motion to dismiss)。
B州有一部“长臂法案” (long-arm statute)，赋予其法院对故意损害B州居民或企业的州外被告人身管辖权。
联邦法院将如何裁定博主的驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为博主知道她的评论会对B州的餐厅产生负面影响。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，除非博主未能随动议附上宣誓书 (affidavit) 以证明为何不存在人身管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为博主从未去过B州。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为博主在A州撰写了该评论。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 管辖权与审判地

正确答案：A。法院将驳回驳回动议，因为博主明知其评论会对B州的餐厅造成负面影响。

核心法律规则

特定属人管辖权 (Specific Personal Jurisdiction)

联邦法院对非居民被告行使特定属人管辖权，必须满足两个条件：

  1. 长臂管辖法 (Long-arm statute)：法院所在州的长臂管辖法授权在特定情况下行使管辖权；且
  2. 正当程序 (Due Process)：行使管辖权符合正当程序要求。

正当程序要求满足以下条件：

  • 原告的诉讼请求与被告在法院所在州的最低限度联系 (minimum contacts)相关或密切相关；并且
  • 行使管辖权符合公平正义 (fair play and substantial justice)的理念。

当被告有意利用 (purposefully avails)该州的保护和利益，使其在该州被起诉是合理可预见的，则存在最低限度联系。即使被告从未实际进入该州，有意利用也可能发生，例如，在某个州实施了意图在法院所在州产生影响的故意侵权行为（效果测试, effects test）。

特定属人管辖权的要求
长臂管辖法 法院所在州的长臂管辖法必须授权在特定情况下行使管辖权。
正当程序

最低限度联系 (Minimum contacts)

  • 有意利用 (Purposeful availment)：被告有意利用法院所在州的法律，使其在该州被起诉是可预见的：
    • 商业流测试 (Stream of commerce test) – 被告将商品投入商业流并采取行动故意针对法院所在州。
    • 效果测试 (Effects test) – 被告在一个州实施了故意侵权行为，意图使其效果在法院所在州感受到。

公平正义 (Fair play & substantial justice)

  • 合理性因素 (Reasonableness factors)：
    • 被告在法院所在州出庭和辩护的负担。
    • 原告获得救济的利益。
    • 法院所在州的利益。
    • 州际司法系统在获得最有效解决争议方面的利益。
    • 各州在促进基本实质性社会政策方面的利益。

案件事实与适用逻辑

本案中，B州的联邦法院对博主行使特定属人管辖权的分析如下：

  1. 长臂管辖法： B州的长臂管辖法授权对故意伤害B州居民或企业的州外被告行使管辖权。博主对B州餐厅的诽谤行为符合这一规定。
  2. 正当程序 — 最低限度联系 (Minimum Contacts)：
    • 有意利用 (Purposeful Availment)： 博主撰写了一篇诽谤性评论，虚假声称B州的餐厅存在害虫并使用动物产品。尽管博主从未去过B州，但她故意针对B州的餐厅所有者，并意图通过其行为在B州产生影响。这构成了对B州利益的有意利用。
    • 效果测试 (Effects Test)： 博主实施了故意侵权行为（诽谤），其意图是让效果在B州感受到（餐厅倒闭）。这满足了效果测试的要求，使得在B州被起诉是合理可预见的。
  3. 正当程序 — 公平正义 (Fair Play and Substantial Justice)： 没有迹象表明在此案中行使管辖权会违背公平正义的理念。

因此，B州联邦法院对博主拥有特定属人管辖权，博主的驳回动议很可能会被驳回。

特定属人管辖权分析流程

是否存在长臂管辖法授权？
➜
是否满足正当程序？
➜
最低限度联系 (Minimum Contacts)？
➜
有意利用 (Purposeful Availment)？
➜
效果测试 (Effects Test) 适用？
➜
公平正义 (Fair Play & Substantial Justice)？
➜
存在属人管辖权

本案中，博主故意侵权行为的目标是B州，满足效果测试，因此B州法院拥有属人管辖权。

陷阱提示：故意侵权与物理存在

MBE考试中一个常见的陷阱是，当被告从未物理进入法院所在州时，考生可能会错误地认为缺乏最低限度联系。然而，对于故意侵权行为 (intentional torts)，即使被告没有物理存在，只要其行为是有意利用 (purposeful availment)法院所在州的利益，并且意图使其效果在该州感受到（即满足效果测试），就可能建立特定属人管辖权。本案中，博主未曾到访B州，但其诽谤行为明确针对B州餐厅，导致其倒闭，这正是效果测试的典型应用。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 驳回驳回动议，因为博主明知其评论会对B州的餐厅造成负面影响。

正确。 这符合效果测试的原则。博主故意撰写诽谤性评论，意图损害B州的餐厅，并且该评论确实在B州产生了负面影响（餐厅倒闭）。这种有意利用和可预见的效果足以建立最低限度联系，从而支持B州法院行使特定属人管辖权。

B. 驳回驳回动议，除非博主未能附上宣誓书以证明属人管辖权不存在。

错误。 尽管在驳回动议中附上宣誓书是常见的程序，但本题的核心是属人管辖权的实质性法律分析，而非程序性细节。即使博主附上了宣誓书，如果根据事实和法律分析，属人管辖权确实存在，动议仍将被驳回。

C. 批准驳回动议，因为博主从未去过B州。

错误。 物理存在并非建立最低限度联系的绝对要求，尤其是在故意侵权行为的背景下。效果测试允许法院在被告从未进入该州的情况下行使管辖权，只要被告的故意行为旨在该州产生效果。

D. 批准驳回动议，因为博主在A州撰写了评论。

错误。 行为发生地（A州）并不决定属人管辖权。关键在于被告的行为是否有意利用了法院所在州（B州）的利益，并意图在该州产生效果。博主在A州撰写评论，但其目标和影响地是B州，因此A州不是唯一的管辖地。

考试技巧：故意侵权与属人管辖权

在MBE考试中，当遇到涉及故意侵权行为（如诽谤、欺诈）的属人管辖权问题时，请重点关注效果测试 (effects test)。即使被告从未物理进入法院所在州，只要其行为是有意利用 (purposeful availment)该州利益，并意图在该州产生可预见的效果，法院通常就能行使特定属人管辖权。不要被被告的物理缺席所迷惑。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A driver from the Western District of State A was involved in a traffic collision in the Northern District of State B with a truck owned and operated by a shipping company incorporated in the Eastern District of State B. The shipping company does the bulk of its business in the Southern District of State B, where its headquarters are located. The employee who drove the truck was terminated by the shipping company. The employee is a resident of State C, which has one federal judicial district.
If the driver files a joint complaint against the shipping company and its former employee, in which federal judicial district(s) would venue be proper?

choices.A: The Western District of State A.
choices.B: The Northern District of State B.
choices.C: The Western District of State A and the Northern District of State B.
choices.D: The Eastern District of State B, the Southern District of State B, and the District of State C.

questions.explanation:
Proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1391)
Proper in all of the following districts:
Residency-based
Events-based
Property-based
OR
Proper in any district with personal jurisdiction over defendant
Service of process
Consent
Specific
(minimum contacts)
General
(domicile)

Venue refers to the federal judicial districts where a case may be heard and can be established in the following ways:

  • Residency-based venue – a district where any defendant resides, if all of the defendants reside in the same state
  • Events-based venue – a district where a substantial part of the events that gave rise to the suit occurred
  • Property-based venue – a district where a substantial part of the property at issue is located (not seen here)
  • Fallback provision – a district where any defendant is subject to the court's personal jurisdiction (only applies if none of the above provisions can be established)

For venue purposes, a corporate defendant (eg, the shipping company) is a resident of any judicial district where it is subject to personal jurisdiction—eg, where it is incorporated or maintains its headquarters.

Here, venue is improper in the Western District of State A (where the driver resides) because venue is never based on the plaintiff's residence (Choices A & C). And residency-based venue does not apply here because the defendants are residents of different states—the company is incorporated and headquartered in State B, while the former employee is a resident of State C (Choice D). However, events-based venue is always available, so venue is proper in the Northern District of State B—where the accident occurred.

📌 Educational Objective

Venue is proper in any federal district where (1) any defendant resides, as long as all defendants reside in the same state, (2) a substantial part of the events occurred, (3) the property at issue is located, or (4) any defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction—but only if venue does not arise under the preceding provisions.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) (proper venue).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：联邦法院审判地

本题考察的核心知识点是美国联邦民事诉讼中的审判地 (Venue) 规则，具体依据为 28 U.S.C. § 1391。

⚖️ 核心法则：审判地三步走
在联邦法院，适当的审判地 (Proper Venue) 通常存在于以下地区：
  1. 居住地原则 (Residency-based)：如果所有被告都居住在同一个州，则该州内的任何一个被告居住的司法区均可。
  2. 事件发生地原则 (Events-based)：产生诉讼请求的重大部分事件 (Substantial part of events) 发生的司法区。
  3. 兜底条款 (Fallback)：仅当前两项都无法确定审判地时，任何被告受法院对人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction) 管辖的司法区。

🧠 案情逻辑分析

第一步：分析被告的居住地

本案有两名被告：

  • 船运公司：在 B 州注册并设总部 ➡️ 视为 B 州居民。
  • 前雇员（司机）：是 C 州居民。

❌ 结论：被告分别居住在 B 州和 C 州（不同州）。因此，不能使用“居住地原则”来确定审判地。这直接排除了基于被告居住地的选项（如选项 D）。

第二步：分析事件发生地

交通事故（即诉讼的起因）发生在 B 州北区 (Northern District of State B)。

✅ 结论：根据“事件发生地原则”，B 州北区是适当的审判地。

第三步：排除原告居住地

原告（司机）居住在 A 州西区。

❌ 结论：在一般联邦审判地规则下，原告的居住地与审判地无关。除非有特殊法规（本题未涉及），否则原告不能仅因自己住在那里就在那里起诉。

🔍 选项深度解析

正确 选项 B：B 州北区

这是事故发生的地点。根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(2)，这是产生诉讼的重大部分事件发生地，因此是适当的审判地。

错误 选项 A & C：涉及 A 州西区

A 州西区仅仅是原告的居住地。审判地规则保护的是被告，防止其被迫在对其不便的地方应诉。原告的居住地通常不是建立审判地的依据。

错误 选项 D：B 州东区/南区 & C 州

这个选项试图利用“居住地原则”，列出了被告所在的区域。但是，该原则有一个严格的前提：所有被告必须居住在同一个州。由于被告分属 B 州和 C 州，该原则完全不适用。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在做 Venue 的题目时，养成条件反射： 1. 先看被告是否都在同一个州？(如果是，选被告居住地) 2. 如果不是，直接找“出事地点” (Events occurred)。 3. 永远不要因为原告住在那里就选原告的居住地（除非是极少数特殊类型的案件，如针对联邦官员的某些诉讼，但 MBE 通常考通用规则）。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman from State A contacted an attorney after she developed a lung disorder, which she claims was caused by e-cigarettes. After researching the woman's claim, the attorney discovered that other individuals across the country developed similar lung disorders from the use of the same brand of e-cigarettes manufactured by a company incorporated and with its principal place of business in State B.
The attorney filed a class action in federal court in State A on behalf of 70 individuals against the company. The woman was the only named plaintiff. Each class member's claim amounted to $100,000, and the damages on behalf of the entire class amount to $7 million. Ten of the unnamed plaintiffs live in State B.
The company filed an answer denying responsibility. Twenty days later, it filed a motion to dismiss the class action for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
How will the court likely rule on the company's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because diversity jurisdiction exists.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the company waived its claim for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction by filing its motion after its answer.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because members of the class and the company are citizens of State B.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the class only contains 70 members.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction in class actions
Type Requirements
Federal question • Class action arises under U.S. Constitution, treaty, or federal law
Diversity • Amount in controversy for any named plaintiff's claim exceeds $75,000* and
• named opposing parties are citizens of different states
Class Action Fairness Act • Class contains ≥ 100 members
• at least one class member & one defendant are diverse and
• amount in controversy for aggregated claims exceeds $5 million

*A federal court can acquire subject-matter jurisdiction over class members' claims that do not exceed $75,000 through supplemental jurisdiction.

A class action is a suit filed by one or more named plaintiffs (ie, class representatives) on behalf of similarly harmed unnamed plaintiffs. As in any other lawsuit, a federal court can obtain subject-matter jurisdiction over a class action through either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – when the class action arises from the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction – when the named opposing parties are citizens of different states (ie, are diverse) and the amount in controversy for any named plaintiff's claim exceeds $75,000.*

Here, the woman from State A (named plaintiff) and the company incorporated and headquartered in State B (named defendant) are diverse. The fact that 10 unnamed plaintiffs are also citizens of State B does not destroy diversity (Choice C). Additionally, the woman—and every other class member—asserted a claim for $100,000, which satisfies the amount-in-controversy requirement. Therefore, the federal court has diversity jurisdiction and will likely deny the company's motion to dismiss.

*A federal court can acquire subject-matter jurisdiction over class members' claims that do not exceed $75,000 through supplemental jurisdiction.

(Choice B) Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(h), a defendant waives certain defenses if they are not asserted in a pre-answer motion or an answer—whichever occurs first. But a defense based on lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived and can be asserted at any time.

(Choice D) The Class Action Fairness Act provides an alternate basis for subject-matter jurisdiction when (1) the class contains at least 100 members, (2) any member is diverse from at least one defendant, and (3) the aggregated amount in controversy exceeds $5 million. This Act does not apply here because the class has only 70 members, but the court still has subject-matter jurisdiction based on diversity.

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court has diversity jurisdiction over a class action when (1) the named opposing parties are citizens of different states and (2) the amount in controversy for any named plaintiff's claim exceeds $75,000.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 23 (class actions).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a) (diversity jurisdiction).
  • Supreme Tribe of Ben-Hur v. Cauble, 255 U.S. 356, 366 (1921) (holding that only the named opposing parties in a class action need to be diverse to satisfy diversity jurisdiction).

一名来自A州的女性在患上一种肺部疾病后联系了一名律师，她声称该疾病是由电子烟引起的。在研究了该女性的诉求后，律师发现全国各地有其他个人也因使用同一品牌的电子烟而患上类似的肺部疾病，该电子烟由一家在B州注册成立且主营业地在B州的公司生产。

该律师在A州的联邦法院代表70名个人对该公司提起了集体诉讼。该女性是唯一的具名原告。每个集体成员的索赔金额为100,000美元，整个集体的损害赔偿总额为700万美元。其中十名非具名原告居住在B州。

该公司提交了否认责任的答辩状。二十天后，该公司以缺乏标的物管辖权为由，提出驳回该集体诉讼的动议。

法院可能会如何裁定公司的该项动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为存在多元管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为该公司在提交答辩状后才提出动议，已放弃了其关于缺乏标的物管辖权的主张。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为集体成员和该公司都是B州的公民。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为该集体仅有70名成员。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Class Action Jurisdiction

核心考点：集体诉讼的管辖权 本题考察联邦法院对集体诉讼（Class Action）行使标的物管辖权（Subject-Matter Jurisdiction, SMJ）的两种途径：
  1. 标准多元管辖权 (Standard Diversity)
  2. 集体诉讼公平法案 (CAFA)

法院将驳回 (Deny) 被告的动议，因为本案满足标准多元管辖权的要求。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

在联邦民事诉讼中，集体诉讼要进入联邦法院，通常需要满足以下两套标准之一：

标准 Standard Diversity
(常规多元性)		 CAFA
(公平法案)
当事人多元性 完全多元 (Complete Diversity)
仅看具名当事人 (Named Parties)		 最低多元 (Minimal Diversity)
任何一名成员 vs 任何一名被告
争议金额 (AIC) > $75,000
(针对具名原告)		 > $5,000,000
(汇总总额)
人数要求 无特定要求 ≥ 100 人

🔍 案情逻辑推演

第一步 检查标准多元管辖权
根据最高法院在 Supreme Tribe of Ben-Hur v. Cauble 案中的判例，对于集体诉讼的多元性判断，只看具名代表 (Named Representative) 的国籍，忽略未具名的集体成员。
  • 具名原告： A州公民。
  • 被告： B州公民（注册地+主营业地）。
  • 结论： A vs B，满足完全多元性。那10个住在B州的未具名原告不影响管辖权。
第二步 检查争议金额
具名原告的索赔额为 $100,000，超过了 $75,000 的法定门槛。
注意：只要具名原告满足金额要求，法院通常可以对其他金额不足的成员行使补充管辖权（Supplemental Jurisdiction），尽管本案中所有人都满足。
结论 既然满足了标准多元管辖权，法院就有权审理。不需要再考虑 CAFA 的要求。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 C 错误 (关于未具名成员)：
虽然有10名未具名原告与被告同属B州，但在集体诉讼的标准多元管辖权分析中，我们只看具名当事人。未具名成员的国籍不会破坏多元性 (Diversity is not destroyed)。
选项 D 错误 (关于 CAFA)：
这个选项试图用 Class Action Fairness Act (CAFA) 的标准来迷惑你。CAFA 确实要求集体成员至少 100 人。但是，CAFA 只是建立管辖权的额外途径，而不是唯一途径。既然本案已经满足了常规的 § 1332 多元管辖权，是否满足 CAFA 就无关紧要了。
选项 B 错误 (关于豁免)：
标的物管辖权 (Subject-Matter Jurisdiction) 永远不会被豁免 (Never Waived)。 即使被告在答辩状 (Answer) 之后才提出动议，法院也必须受理该动议。如果法院发现缺乏 SMJ，必须随时驳回案件。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An investor from State A sued a company from State B in a federal court. The investor's complaint asserted a misrepresentation claim for $40,000 and a breach-of-contract claim for $40,000. The claims arose from unrelated investments that the investor made in the company.
The company moved to dismiss the complaint for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Is the court likely to grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because original jurisdiction exists over the claims.
choices.B: No, because supplemental jurisdiction exists over the claims.
choices.C: Yes, because neither claim independently satisfies the amount-in-controversy requirement.
choices.D: Yes, because the claims arose from unrelated investments.

questions.explanation:
Amount in controversy
(aggregation of claims)
Procedural
posture		 Claims asserted Outcome
One π v. one Δ • Negligence – $40K
• Battery – $60K 		• Aggregation allowed
• Amount in controversy = $100K
One π v.
multiple Δs		 • Negligence against Δ1 – $40K
• Battery against Δ2 – $60K 		• Aggregation not allowed unless Δs jointly liable
• Amounts in controversy = $40K & $60K
Multiple πs v.
one Δ		 π1 asserts negligence – $40K
π2 asserts battery – $60K 		• Aggregation not allowed unless πs enforcing common or undivided interest
• Amounts in controversy = $40K & $60K
π1 asserts negligence – $40K
π1 asserts breach of contract – $40K
π2 asserts battery – $60K 		• Aggregation allowed for π1's claims
• Aggregation not allowed for π2's claim
• Amounts in controversy = $80K & $60K

π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant.

A federal court has the authority to hear a case or controversy if it falls within the court's original subject-matter jurisdiction. Original jurisdiction is established through either:

• federal-question jurisdiction – when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or

• diversity jurisdiction – when the opposing parties are citizens of different states (ie, are diverse) and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

The amount in controversy is the amount demanded in the plaintiff's complaint, excluding interest and costs. To meet the required amount, a single plaintiff can aggregate (ie, combine) any claims asserted against a single defendant. This is true even if those claims are legally and/or factually unrelated—eg, the investor's claims that arose from unrelated investments (Choice D).*

Here, the investor and the company are diverse since they are from States A and B, respectively. Neither of the investor's claims independently exceeds $75,000. But since the claims are asserted against a single defendant, they can be aggregated to $80,000 to satisfy the amount-in-controversy requirement (Choice C). As a result, original jurisdiction exists over the claims, and the federal court will likely deny the company's motion to dismiss.

*FRCP 42 allows a federal court to order separate trials of related and/or unrelated claims for convenience, to avoid prejudice, or to expedite and economize.

(Choice B) A federal court may exercise supplemental jurisdiction to hear certain claims that do not arise under the court's original jurisdiction—ie, federal-question or diversity jurisdiction. But here, supplemental jurisdiction need not be analyzed since the court has diversity jurisdiction over the aggregated claims.

📌 Educational Objective

To meet the amount-in-controversy requirement for diversity jurisdiction (excess of $75,000), a single plaintiff can aggregate (ie, combine) his/her claims against a single defendant—even if those claims are unrelated.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction

正确答案：A

否，因为法院对这些诉讼请求拥有初始管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)。

法院很可能会驳回被告的动议，因为原告通过合并两个诉讼请求，满足了联邦法院多元管辖权的要求。

核心考点：争议金额的合并

Aggregation of Amount in Controversy

联邦法院行使多元管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction) 必须满足两个条件：

  1. 完全多元性 (Complete Diversity)：原告和被告必须是不同州的公民。
  2. 争议金额 (Amount in Controversy)：必须超过 $75,000。
关键规则：单一原告 vs. 单一被告

为了满足 $75,000 的门槛，单一原告 (Single Plaintiff) 可以将其针对单一被告 (Single Defendant) 的所有诉讼请求金额进行合并计算 (Aggregate)。

⚠️ 重要细节：这些诉讼请求不需要在法律上或事实上相关 (Unrelated claims are okay)。

本案分析

1. 多元性分析：
原告来自 A 州，被告来自 B 州。满足完全多元性。

2. 金额分析：
原告提出了两项请求：

  • 虚假陈述 (Misrepresentation): $40,000
  • 违约 (Breach of Contract): $40,000
$40,000 + $40,000 = $80,000

结论：
$80,000 > $75,000。因此满足争议金额要求。法院拥有初始管辖权 (Original Jurisdiction)。

MBE 必背：合并计算规则表

情形 规则
1 原告 vs. 1 被告 ✅ 可以合并所有请求（无论是否相关）。
1 原告 vs. 多被告 ❌ 不可合并（除非被告承担连带责任 Joint Liability）。
多原告 vs. 1 被告 ❌ 不可合并（除非原告主张共同/不可分割的利益 Common/Undivided Interest）。

易错点辨析

为什么不选 B (补充管辖权 Supplemental Jurisdiction)？

这是一个常见的干扰项。补充管辖权通常用于将一个“不够格”的请求（例如金额不足或非联邦问题）挂靠在一个“够格”的请求上。

在本案中，通过合并计算，整个案件本身就已经满足了多元管辖权的要求，构成了初始管辖权。因此，不需要动用补充管辖权分析。

为什么不选 D (不相关的投资)？

题目特意提到“不相关的投资”是为了迷惑考生。在 1对1 (单一原告对单一被告) 的情况下，诉讼请求是否相关完全不影响金额的合并。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A photographer sued a foreign publisher in a federal district court in State A for copyright infringement. The photographer followed the foreign country's service of process rules to serve the publisher with a copy of the summons and complaint. The publisher has never been to State A and conducts no business there.
The publisher filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss the case for improper service of process. The district court denied this motion. Twelve days after receiving notice of the denial, the publisher filed and served an answer that included a motion to dismiss the case for lack of personal jurisdiction.
Is the court likely to grant the publisher's motion?

choices.A: No, because the publisher failed to file and serve his answer within 10 days after receiving notice of the court's denial of his pre-answer motion.
choices.B: No, because the publisher waived any objection to personal jurisdiction.
choices.C: Yes, because the publisher has never physically traveled to State A and conducts no business there.
choices.D: Yes, because the publisher properly filed and served his answer.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Waiver of defenses
Defenses Waiver
• Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction Never waived
• Lack of personal jurisdiction
• Improper venue
• Insufficient process or service of process 		Waived if not asserted in pre-answer motion or answer (whichever occurs first)
• Failure to state claim
• Failure to join required party 		Waived if not asserted before end of trial
• All other legal defenses Waived if not asserted in answer or amended answer

Personal jurisdiction is a court's authority over the parties or property before it. One way to establish personal jurisdiction is through the parties' consent. A plaintiff consents to the court's jurisdiction by filing the complaint in that court. In contrast, a defendant can consent in any of the following ways:

  • Express consent – by contractually agreeing to the court's jurisdiction (eg, forum-selection clause)
  • Implied consent – by engaging in an activity that the forum state has a substantial interest in regulating (eg, driving on public roads)
  • Waiver – by failing to assert a personal-jurisdiction objection in a pre-answer motion or answer, whichever occurs first

Here, the publisher filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss for improper* service of process. But he previously waived any objection to personal jurisdiction by failing to assert this objection in his pre-answer motion. As a result, the publisher consented to the court's jurisdiction, and the court will likely deny his motion to dismiss.

*Service of process is proper here because a foreign defendant can be served by following the foreign country's rules for service of process.

(Choices A & D) If the defendant files a pre-answer motion, the defendant must file and serve an answer within 14 days after receiving notice of the court's denial or postponement of that motion—as the publisher did here. Nevertheless, the publisher waived his personal-jurisdiction defense by failing to assert it in his pre-answer motion.

(Choice C) The fact that the publisher has never physically traveled to State A and conducts no business there shows that the court cannot establish personal jurisdiction over him through specific jurisdiction. However, it can still establish personal jurisdiction through the publisher's consent.

📌 Educational Objective

A court can acquire personal jurisdiction through the defendant's consent—ie, express consent, implied consent, or waiver. A defendant waives a personal-jurisdiction objection by failing to assert it in a pre-answer motion or answer, whichever occurs first.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(h)(1) (waiver of personal-jurisdiction defense).

该出版商提交了一份答辩前动议，以送达程序不当为由请求驳回案件。地区法院驳回了此动议。在收到驳回通知十二天后，该出版商提交并送达了一份答辩状，其中包含了以缺乏对人管辖权为由请求驳回案件的动议。

法院是否可能批准该出版商的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为出版商未能在收到法院驳回其答辩前动议的通知后 10 天内提交并送达其答辩状。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为出版商放弃了任何对对人管辖权的异议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为出版商从未亲身到过 A 州，也未在该州开展任何业务。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为出版商恰当地提交并送达了他的答辩状。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Waiver of Defenses

本题考察的是美国联邦民事诉讼规则（FRCP）中关于抗辩权的放弃（Waiver of Defenses）这一核心概念，特别是 Rule 12(g) 和 12(h)。

核心规则：Rule 12 "Use it or Lose it" 如果被告决定提交答辩前动议（Pre-answer Motion），他必须将所有当时可用的 Rule 12(b)(2)-(5) 抗辩理由合并在这一次动议中提出。如果遗漏了，这些抗辩理由即被视为永久放弃（Waived）。

1. 哪些抗辩必须一次性提出？

以下四种抗辩被称为“可放弃的抗辩”（Waivable Defenses），必须在被告的第一次回应（无论是动议还是答辩状）中提出：

抗辩理由 (Defense) FRCP 条款
缺乏对人管辖权
Lack of Personal Jurisdiction		 12(b)(2)
审判地不当
Improper Venue		 12(b)(3)
传票内容不充分
Insufficient Process		 12(b)(4)
送达程序不充分
Insufficient Service		 12(b)(5)

2. 案情分析

第一步：被告的第一次行动

出版商选择提交了一个答辩前动议（Pre-answer motion）。在这个动议中，他只提出了送达程序不当（Improper service）。

第二步：致命的遗漏

在提交第一个动议时，出版商本可以同时提出“缺乏对人管辖权”（Lack of Personal Jurisdiction）的抗辩，但他没有这样做。

第三步：法律后果

根据 Rule 12(h)(1)，因为他在第一个动议中遗漏了对人管辖权的抗辩，该抗辩权已经消失。即使他在随后的答辩状（Answer）中试图补救，也为时已晚。

3. 为什么其他选项是错误的？

❌ 选项 A (关于时间)：
虽然 Rule 12(a)(4) 规定如果动议被驳回，被告通常有 14 天时间提交答辩状。本案中被告在 12 天后提交，时间上是合规的。但问题不在于时间，而在于内容的放弃。

❌ 选项 C (关于管辖权实质)：
这是一个典型的“陷阱选项”。虽然出版商从未去过 A 州（Minimum Contacts 分析），这通常意味着法院确实没有管辖权。但是，程序规则优先于实质权利。因为被告未能及时提出异议，他被视为同意（Consented）了法院的管辖权。即使他在实体法上有理，程序上的失误也是致命的。

❌ 选项 D (认为程序正确)：
虽然答辩状本身提交得恰当，但其中包含的“驳回动议”是基于一个已经放弃的理由。因此法院不会批准该动议。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip) 在 MBE 中，一旦看到被告提交了 Pre-answer Motion，立即检查他是否遗漏了上述四个“可放弃抗辩”中的任何一个。如果遗漏了，该抗辩就死了，后续再提也没用。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Plaintiff, a new homeowner, entered into a contract with the defendants, a designer and an architect. The contract required the defendants to remodel the plaintiff's home in State A. The designer resides in the Eastern District of State B, and the architect resides in the Western District of State B.
The defendants failed to do any of the work, so the plaintiff sued them together in a federal court in the Eastern District of State B.
The defendants filed a motion to dismiss for improper venue.
Will the federal court likely grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because both defendants are subject to personal jurisdiction in State B.
choices.B: No, because the designer resides in the Eastern District of State B and the architect resides in the Western District of State B.
choices.C: Yes, because the contract was to be performed at the plaintiff's home in State A.
choices.D: Yes, because the architect resides in the Western District of State B.

questions.explanation:
Requirements for proper federal court
Subject-matter jurisdiction
Can plaintiff bring claim in federal court?
We the People
OR
👤
Personal jurisdiction
Is defendant sufficiently connected to forum state?
Eg, state of residence
Eg, minimum contacts
$
Venue
In which forum-state district can claim be heard?
Eg, residency-based
👤🏠
Eg, events-based
🚚🚗

Venue—ie, the geographical location of the federal court that can hear a lawsuit—is proper in any judicial district where:

  • any defendant resides—so long as all defendants reside in the same state (ie, residency-based venue)
  • a substantial portion of the events that gave rise to the suit occurred (ie, events-based venue) or a substantial part of the property at issue is located (ie, property-based venue) or
  • any defendant is subject to the court's personal jurisdiction—but only if neither of the above provisions applies (ie, fallback provision).

Here, both defendants reside in State B. And since the designer resides in the Eastern District of State B, residency-based venue exists there. The fact that venue would also be proper in the Western District of State B (since the architect resides there) does not negate the proper venue in the Eastern District of State B (Choice D). Therefore, the court will likely deny the defendants' motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) Whether a defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction will only be considered for venue purposes if (1) the defendant is a corporation (since it resides where it is subject to personal jurisdiction) or (2) the fallback provision applies because residency, events, and property-based venue cannot be shown. Neither instance is seen here.

(Choice C) State A is a proper, events-based venue because the contract giving rise to the suit was to be performed there. But venue can be proper in multiple judicial districts—including the Eastern District of State B.

📌 Educational Objective

Venue is proper in any federal district where (1) any defendant resides so long as all defendants reside in the same state, (2) a substantial portion of the events occurred or a substantial part of the property is located, or (3) any defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction—but only if the first two provisions do not exist.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) (proper venue).
questions.zh-question:
原告，一名新房主，与被告，即一名设计师和一名建筑师，签订了一份合同。该合同要求被告在A州对原告的房屋进行改造。该设计师居住在B州东区，而建筑师居住在B州西区。

被告未能履行任何工作，因此原告在B州东区的联邦法院对他们一并提起了诉讼。

被告以审判地（venue）不当为由，提起了驳回动议（motion to dismiss）。

联邦法院是否可能批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为两名被告均受B州的对人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）管辖。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为设计师居住在B州东区，而建筑师居住在B州西区。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为合同将在A州的原告家中履行。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为建筑师居住在B州西区。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析
联邦民事诉讼法：审判地
✅ 正确答案：选项 B
法院不会批准动议，因为审判地适当。
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (The Rule)

本题考察的是 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1) 关于基于居住地的审判地 (Residency-Based Venue) 的规定。

在联邦民事诉讼中，如果所有被告都居住在同一个州 (State)，则该州的任何一个被告居住的司法区 (Judicial District) 都是适当的审判地。

🔍 案情应用 (Application)
1. 确定被告居住地：
设计师住在 B 州东区 (Eastern District of State B)。
建筑师住在 B 州西区 (Western District of State B)。
2. 检查是否同州：
两名被告都居住在 B 州。条件满足。
3. 确定适当审判地：
根据规则，B 州的任何包含被告居住地的区域都是适当的。因此，B 州东区（设计师居住地）和 B 州西区（建筑师居住地）均为适当审判地 (Proper Venue)。

因此，原告在 B 州东区起诉是完全合法的，法院不会因为审判地不当而驳回起诉。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (Personal Jurisdiction)：
虽然被告确实受 B 州管辖，但审判地 (Venue) 和对人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction) 是两个不同的概念。除非没有其他适用的审判地规则（即适用 Fallback Provision），否则不直接用“管辖权”来决定审判地。
选项 C (Events-Based Venue)：
A 州确实也是一个适当的审判地（因为合同履行地/事件发生地在 A 州），但这并不意味着 B 州就是不当的。一个案件可以有多个适当的审判地。
选项 D (Western District)：
虽然 B 州西区也是适当的，但这并不排斥 B 州东区的适当性。只要符合规则，原告可以在多个适当的审判地中任选其一。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A businesswoman sued a website owner in federal court for violating federal copyright law. The businesswoman sent a copy of the complaint and a form requesting waiver of service of process to the website owner's residence via first-class mail. The request named the court where the complaint was filed and the date when the request was sent.
The businesswoman did not receive anything back from the website owner, so 31 days after mailing the request, she had a process server hand-deliver a copy of the summons and complaint to the website owner.
Is the website owner liable for the expenses associated with the process server?

choices.A: No, because the businesswoman did not include all that was necessary for a waiver request.
choices.B: No, because the businesswoman did not wait 60 days before hiring the process server.
choices.C: Yes, because a court must impose the cost of service upon a defendant who fails to waive service.
choices.D: Yes, because a defendant has a duty to avoid unnecessary service-of-process expenses.

questions.explanation:
Waiving service of process
(FRCP 4(d))
Request for waiver
  • In writing
  • Addressed to defendant (or authorized agent)
  • Names court where complaint filed
  • Provides copy of complaint, two waiver forms & prepaid means to return form
  • Informs defendant about consequences of waiving & not waiving
  • Lists date request is sent
  • Sent via first-class mail or other reliable means
  • Allows 30 days (or 60 days for defendant abroad) from date sent for defendant to return waiver
Benefits of waiver
  • Defendant's time to file answer extended to 60 days (or 90 days if abroad) from date sent
Consequences of failing to waive
  • Defendant pays expenses of future service of process
  • Defendant pays reasonable expenses of any motion required to collect service expenses (eg, attorney's fees)

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A plaintiff must provide the defendant with adequate notice of a lawsuit through service of process—ie, by delivering a copy of the summons and complaint. Since this can be expensive and burdensome, defendants are encouraged to waive service of process upon the plaintiff's written request. That request must:

  • be sent to the defendant via first-class mail or other reliable means
  • name the court where the complaint was filed and the date the request was sent and
  • contain one copy of the complaint, two copies of the waiver form, and a prepaid means for returning the signed waiver form (eg, a self-addressed and stamped envelope).

If the defendant waives service of process, the defendant receives extra time to respond to the complaint—60 days from the date the request was sent instead of 21 days from the date of service (the carrot). But if the defendant (1) fails to waive service and (2) lacks good cause for doing so, the defendant must pay the expenses of future service and of any motion required to collect those expenses (the stick).

Here, the businesswoman's waiver request only contained one copy of the waiver form and did not include a prepaid means to return the signed form. Therefore, the website owner is not liable for the process-server expenses (Choices C & D).

(Choice B) A plaintiff must give a defendant reasonable time to return the waiver—ie, at least 30 days when the defendant is in the U.S. (as seen here) or at least 60 days if the defendant is abroad.

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff must send a written waiver-of-service request to the defendant via first-class mail or other reliable means. The waiver must state the name of the court and the date the request was sent. It also must contain a copy of the complaint, two copies of the waiver form, and a prepaid means to return the signed form.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(d) (waiving service of process).
questions.zh-question:
一名女商人因网站所有者违反联邦版权法在联邦法院对其提起诉讼。该女商人通过一类邮件向网站所有者的住所寄送了一份诉状副本和一份请求放弃传票送达的表格。该请求指明了受理诉状的法院以及请求发出的日期。

该女商人未收到网站所有者的任何回复，因此在寄出请求31天后，她雇佣了一名送达员将传票和诉状的副本亲手送达给网站所有者。

网站所有者是否对与送达员相关的费用承担责任？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为女商人的放弃请求书中未包含所有必要文件。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为女商人在雇佣送达员前没有等待60天。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法院必须将送达费用判由未能放弃送达的被告承担。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为被告有义务避免不必要的传票送达费用。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Service of Process
正确答案：A

否，因为女商人的放弃请求书中未包含所有必要文件。

被告无需支付送达费用的原因是原告发出的放弃送达请求（Waiver Request）在程序上存在瑕疵。

核心考点：FRCP 4(d) 放弃送达

联邦民事诉讼规则（FRCP 4(d)）鼓励被告放弃正式的传票送达（Service of Process）以节省司法资源。如果被告无正当理由拒绝放弃，必须承担后续的送达费用。

但是！这一惩罚机制生效的前提是：原告必须严格遵守请求放弃的所有程序要求。

有效请求的必备要素 (Checklist)
  • 书面形式并寄给被告本人
  • 通过一类邮件 (First-class mail) 或其他可靠方式发送
  • 指明法院名称和发送日期
  • 附带诉状副本 (Copy of complaint)
  • 附带两份放弃表格 (Two copies of waiver form)
  • 附带预付邮资的回邮工具 (Prepaid means of compliance)
本题陷阱分析 题目中提到原告寄送了 "a form"（一份表格），且未提及 "prepaid envelope"（预付邮资信封）。

由于原告未能提供两份表格（一份供被告寄回，一份供被告留存）和回邮信封，该请求在程序上是无效的。因此，被告没有义务放弃送达，也就无需承担后续费用。
为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 B (关于60天)：
这是一个常见的时间混淆点。

  • 30天：原告必须给予被告至少30天的时间来决定是否放弃（从寄出请求之日算起）。本题中原告等待了31天，时间上是合规的。
  • 60天：如果被告同意放弃，被告有60天的时间（从请求寄出之日算起）来提交答辩状（Answer），而不是通常的21天。
结论：原告不需要等待60天再雇佣送达员，只要过了给被告的合理考虑期（30天）即可。

选项 C & D (关于被告义务)：
这两个选项陈述了一般原则（被告有义务避免不必要的费用），但忽略了前提条件：原告的请求必须完美合规。如果原告自己都没把程序做对，法院不会惩罚被告。

💡 MBE 考试技巧 在涉及 FRCP 4(d) Waiver of Service 的题目中，如果问“被告是否需要支付费用”，请立即检查原告寄出的包裹里是否包含：
  1. 两份表格 (Two copies)
  2. 预付邮资的信封 (Prepaid envelope)
如果缺了任何一个，原告就输了，被告无需付费。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A shop owner domiciled in State A sued a distributor in a federal district court in State A for breach of a contract. The shop owner sought $100,000 in damages for allegedly defective goods that the distributor had provided under the contract. The distributor is incorporated in State B, with its principal place of business in State C. The distributor brought in as a third-party defendant the wholesaler that had provided the goods to the distributor, alleging that the wholesaler had a duty to indemnify the distributor for any damages recovered by the shop owner. The wholesaler is incorporated in State B, with its principal place of business in State A.
The wholesaler has asserted a $60,000 counterclaim against the distributor for payment for the goods at issue, and the distributor has moved to dismiss the counterclaim for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Should the motion to dismiss be granted?

choices.A: No, because the wholesaler's and the distributor's principal places of business are diverse.
choices.B: No, because there is supplemental jurisdiction over the wholesaler's counterclaim.
choices.C: Yes, because there is no diversity of citizenship between the distributor and the wholesaler.
choices.D: Yes, because there is no diversity of citizenship between the shop owner and the wholesaler.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction over related claims
Original claim
(>$75,000 + diversity)
Indemnity claim & counterclaim
(same occurrence = supplemental)
Shop owner
(State A)
→
Distributor
(States B & C)
→
Wholesaler
(States A & B)
←
←

Subject-matter jurisdiction generally arises from either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – when the claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or a federal law (not seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction – when the opposing parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

Here, the court has diversity jurisdiction over the shop owner's (citizen of State A) $100,000 claim against the distributor (citizen of States B and C). But the court lacks diversity jurisdiction over the distributor's indemnity claim against the wholesaler because they are both incorporated in State B (Choice A). And it lacks diversity jurisdiction over the wholesaler's counterclaim since it seeks only $60,000.

When a claim does not satisfy subject-matter jurisdiction, supplemental jurisdiction may exist if the claim shares a common nucleus of operative facts as a claim originally within the court's subject-matter jurisdiction. Here, the distributor's indemnity claim and the wholesaler's counterclaim arise from the same defective goods as the shop owner's original diversity claim. But when the original claim is based solely on diversity jurisdiction, supplemental jurisdiction is not permitted if the supplemental claim:

  • would contaminate diversity of citizenship between the opposing plaintiffs and defendants or
  • seeks $75,000 or less and is made by a plaintiff (1) against parties added through joinder, intervention, or impleader or (2) seeking to join through compulsory joinder or intervention.

Here, the distributor's and wholesaler's lack of diversity would not contaminate the diversity between the shop owner and the distributor (Choice C). Although the shop owner and the wholesaler are both citizens of State A, they are not opposing parties because they have asserted no claims against each other (Choice D). And since the wholesaler's $60,000 counterclaim was asserted by a third-party defendant, the court has supplemental jurisdiction over it and should deny the distributor's motion to dismiss.

📌 Educational Objective

A court is generally permitted to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over a claim that does not satisfy subject-matter jurisdiction when that claim shares a common nucleus of operative facts as a claim originally within the court's subject-matter jurisdiction.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1367 (supplemental jurisdiction).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1331 (federal-question jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
一名住所地在A州的店主，因一份合同违约，在A州联邦地区法院起诉了一名分销商。该店主就分销商根据合同提供的据称有缺陷的货物，寻求10万美元的损害赔偿。该分销商在B州注册成立，其主要营业地在C州。分销商将向其提供货物的批发商作为第三方被告带入诉讼，声称批发商有义务就店主获得的任何损害赔偿对分销商进行补偿。该批发商在B州注册成立，其主要营业地在A州。

批发商对分销商提起了6万美元的反诉，要求支付涉案货物的款项，而分销商已动议以缺乏标的物管辖权为由驳回该反诉。

该驳回动议应否被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为批发商和分销商的主要营业地是不同的。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为法院对批发商的反诉拥有补充管辖权。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为分销商和批发商之间不存在公民身份多元化。
zh-choices.D: 应该，因为店主和批发商之间不存在公民身份多元化。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 民事诉讼法解析

Supplemental Jurisdiction & Impleader
正确答案：B 不应批准驳回动议，因为法院对批发商的反诉拥有补充管辖权 (Supplemental Jurisdiction)。
核心考点解析

本题考察的是联邦法院的补充管辖权 (Supplemental Jurisdiction, 28 U.S.C. § 1367) 在第三方诉讼 (Impleader) 中的应用。

基础背景：
原始诉讼（店主 v. 分销商）基于多元化管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction)。

问题焦点：
批发商（第三方被告）对分销商（被告/第三方原告）提起的反诉，是否需要独立的管辖权基础？
逻辑推导步骤
1
检查独立管辖权：
批发商的反诉金额仅为 $60,000（低于 $75,000），且批发商与分销商均为 B 州公民（无多元化）。因此，该反诉没有独立的联邦管辖权基础。
2
检查补充管辖权 (§ 1367(a))：
该反诉是否与原始诉讼源于“共同的核心事实” (Common Nucleus of Operative Fact)？
是的。 它们都涉及同一批有缺陷的货物。因此，法院原则上拥有补充管辖权。
3
检查例外限制 (§ 1367(b))：
这是 MBE 的常考陷阱。在仅基于多元化管辖权的案件中，§ 1367(b) 禁止原告 (Plaintiff) 对根据 Rule 14 (Impleader) 加入的当事人行使补充管辖权。
关键判断：
本案中提出反诉的是批发商（第三方被告），而不是原始原告（店主）。
因此，§ 1367(b) 的限制不适用。

结论： 既然满足了 § 1367(a) 且不受 § 1367(b) 限制，法院对该反诉拥有补充管辖权，即使双方没有多元化公民身份且金额不足。

为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 A (错误)： 提到“主要营业地不同”。这具有误导性。虽然主要营业地不同，但它们都在 B 州注册成立 (Incorporated)，因此在法律上它们都是 B 州公民，不存在多元化。
  • 选项 C (错误)： 认为“缺乏多元化”就应驳回。这是错误的，因为补充管辖权正是为了解决缺乏独立管辖权（如缺乏多元化）但案情相关的诉求而存在的。
  • 选项 D (错误)： 提到店主和批发商之间无多元化。这在本题中不相关，因为店主并没有起诉批发商，批发商也没有起诉店主。他们不是对立当事人。
MBE 考试技巧
在处理 Supplemental Jurisdiction 题目时，请记住口诀：
  1. 关联性 (Relatedness)： 索赔是否源于同一交易或事件？(如果是，进入下一步)
  2. 原告限制 (Plaintiff Limitation)： 原始案件是否仅基于 Diversity？如果是，提出该补充索赔的人是原告吗？
    • 如果是原告针对第三方被告提出的 -> 无管辖权 (除非独立满足条件)。
    • 如果是被告或第三方被告提出的 -> 通常有管辖权。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman from State A was hit in State B by a driver who is a citizen and resident of a foreign country. The driver frequently visited family in State A. Each state is composed of only one federal judicial district.
If the woman files a diversity action against the driver in the federal court in State A, which of the following is the woman's strongest argument that venue is proper?

choices.A: Venue is proper in any judicial district because the driver resides in a foreign country.
choices.B: Venue is proper in any judicial district because the Federal Tort Claims Act applies.
choices.C: Venue is proper in State A because that is where the woman resides.
choices.D: Venue is proper in State A because the driver is subject to personal jurisdiction there.

questions.explanation:
Special rules for where venue is proper
Removal • Federal district where state action was pending
Foreign resident • Any judicial district
Federal official sued in official capacity • Where defendant resides
• Where substantial events occurred or property is located
• Where plaintiff resides if no real property is involved in suit
Foreign government • Where substantial events occurred or property is located
• In federal district court of Washington, D.C.
Multiparty, multforum litigation • Where defendant resides
• Where substantial part of accident occurred
Federal Tort Claims Act • Where plaintiff resides
• Where act/omission occurred

Venue is the geographic location of a federal district court where a case may be heard. Under the general venue statute, venue is proper in a judicial district where:

  • any defendant resides—but only if all defendants reside in the same state
  • a substantial portion of the events occurred or a substantial part of the property at issue is located or
  • any defendant is subject to the court's personal jurisdiction—but only if venue cannot be established under the above provisions.

However, special venue rules apply in certain situations, including when a defendant is a nonresident of the U.S. In this situation, venue is proper in any judicial district.* And since the driver is a resident of a foreign country, this is the woman's strongest argument that venue is proper in State A.

*Additionally, when a non-U.S. resident is joined (ie, added) as a defendant, the non-U.S. resident is disregarded when determining proper venue as to the other defendants in the action.

(Choice B) The Federal Tort Claims Act applies to suits brought against the U.S. government for the tortious conduct of a federal employee—not suits against a nonresident for his/her tortious conduct (as seen here). But had the Act applied, venue would be proper only in the judicial district where the plaintiff resides (State A) or where the act or omission occurred (State B).

(Choice C) Venue is never based on the plaintiff's residence unless the Federal Tort Claims Act applies or a federal officer or employee is sued in his/her official capacity or under color of legal authority—none of which is seen here. Therefore, the woman cannot successfully argue that venue is proper based on where she resides.

(Choice D) Since venue is proper in any judicial district in an action against a non-U.S. resident, personal jurisdiction has no bearing on where venue is proper.

📌 Educational Objective

Venue is the geographic location of a federal district court where a case may be heard. When a defendant is a nonresident of the U.S., venue is proper in any federal judicial district.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391(c)(3) (setting forth the proper venue for non-U.S. residents).
questions.zh-question: 一名来自A州的女子在B州被一名外国公民和居民的司机撞伤。该司机经常在A州探亲。每个州只包含一个联邦司法区。如果该女子在A州的联邦法院对司机提起一项基于多元化管辖权（diversity action）的诉讼，以下哪项是该女子主张管辖地（venue）适当的最有力论据？

zh-choices.A: 管辖地（venue）在任何司法区都适当，因为司机居住在一个外国。
zh-choices.B: 管辖地（venue）在任何司法区都适当，因为《联邦侵权索赔法》（Federal Tort Claims Act）适用。
zh-choices.C: 管辖地（venue）在A州适当，因为那是该女子居住的地方。
zh-choices.D: 管辖地（venue）在A州适当，因为司机在那里受人身管辖权（personal jurisdiction）的约束。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 管辖与审判地

正确答案: A. 当被告是外国居民时，审判地在任何司法区都是适当的。

核心法律规则

审判地 (Venue) 是联邦法院审理案件的地理位置。根据一般审判地法规 (general venue statute)，审判地在以下司法区是适当的：

  • 任何被告 居住 (resides) 的司法区——但仅限于所有被告都居住在同一州的情况下。
  • 发生实质性事件或财产所在地点的司法区。
  • 任何被告受法院 属人管辖 (personal jurisdiction) 的司法区——但仅当根据上述规定无法确定审判地时。

然而，在某些情况下，特殊审判地规则 (special venue rules) 适用，包括当被告是非美国居民时。在这种情况下，根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391(c)(3)，审判地在任何司法区都是适当的。

*此外，当非美国居民作为被告加入诉讼时，在确定其他被告的适当审判地时，该非美国居民的居住地不予考虑。

概念对比表格

情况 审判地适当的地点
移除 (Removal) 州诉讼待决的联邦司法区
外国居民 (Foreign resident) 任何司法区
联邦官员以官方身份被起诉 (Federal official sued in official capacity)
  • 被告居住地
  • 发生实质性事件或财产所在地
  • 若不涉及不动产，原告居住地
外国政府 (Foreign government)
  • 发生实质性事件或财产所在地
  • 华盛顿特区的联邦地区法院
多方、多论坛诉讼 (Multiparty, multiforum litigation)
  • 被告居住地
  • 事故发生实质性部分所在地
联邦侵权索赔法 (Federal Tort Claims Act)
  • 原告居住地
  • 行为/不行为发生地

事实与适用逻辑

本案中，一名州A的女性在州B被一名司机撞伤。关键事实是，该司机是外国公民和居民，即非美国居民。

根据联邦审判地法规的特殊规定 (28 U.S.C. § 1391(c)(3))，当被告是非美国居民时，审判地在任何司法区都是适当的。

因此，尽管司机可能经常访问州A，且州A是原告的居住地，但最强的论点是基于被告的外国居民身份，这使得州A（或任何其他司法区）成为适当的审判地。

图示：审判地确定流程 (非美国居民被告)

确定被告身份
↓
是否为非美国居民？
↓ (是)
审判地在任何司法区
↑ (否)
适用一般审判地规则

陷阱警示

MBE陷阱： 考生常将一般审判地规则与特殊审判地规则混淆。对于非美国居民被告，其居住地（即使在外国）或其在某个州是否受属人管辖，都不影响审判地可以在任何司法区这一特殊规则的适用。不要被被告在某个州的频繁访问或属人管辖信息所迷惑，这些信息可能与一般审判地规则相关，但在此特殊情况下不适用。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 审判地在任何司法区都是适当的，因为司机是外国居民。

正确。 根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391(c)(3)，当被告是外国居民时，审判地在任何司法区都是适当的。这是本案中最直接且最强的论点。

B. 审判地在任何司法区都是适当的，因为联邦侵权索赔法适用。

错误。 联邦侵权索赔法 (Federal Tort Claims Act) 适用于针对美国政府的侵权诉讼，而非针对外国居民的侵权诉讼。因此，该法不适用于本案。

C. 审判地在州A是适当的，因为那是该女性的居住地。

错误。 审判地通常不以原告的居住地为基础，除非在联邦侵权索赔法适用或联邦官员以官方身份被起诉的情况下。本案不属于这些例外情况，因此原告不能仅凭其居住地来主张州A是适当的审判地。

D. 审判地在州A是适当的，因为司机在那里受属人管辖。

错误。 属人管辖 (personal jurisdiction) 与审判地 (venue) 是两个不同的概念。虽然被告在州A可能受属人管辖（例如，通过频繁访问），但当被告是非美国居民时，审判地可以在任何司法区，属人管辖的存在与否不影响这一特殊规则的适用。属人管辖是法院对当事人行使权力的能力，而审判地是案件审理的地理位置。

考试技巧

快速判断： 在审判地问题中，一旦识别出被告是非美国居民，立即想到特殊规则：审判地在任何司法区都适当。这通常是这类问题的正确答案，并且会排除掉许多基于一般规则的干扰项。

参考资料

  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391(c)(3) (规定非美国居民的适当审判地)

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A federal government employee, a citizen of State A, was driving home after his shift in State B when he lost control of his automobile and hit a pedestrian, a citizen of State C. The employee has never been to State C.
The pedestrian filed a negligence suit against the employee in federal court in State C to recover $80,000 in damages. The employee filed a motion to dismiss the action based on improper venue. The pedestrian responded that venue was proper in State C, where she resides, because the employee works for the federal government.
If the court grants the employee's motion, what is the likely explanation?

choices.A: A federal government employee cannot be sued where the plaintiff resides.
choices.B: The employee must be sued in State A, where he resides.
choices.C: The pedestrian sued the employee in his individual capacity.
choices.D: The suit does not arise under a federal statute.

questions.explanation:
Proper venue for suit against federal officer or employee
Official capacity
(recovery from government)		 Special venue rules permit suit in district where:
  • any Δ resides
  • substantial portion of events occurred or property located
  • π resides if no real property involved
Individual capacity
(recovery from officer/employee)		 General venue statute permits suit in district where:
  • any Δ resides, if all Δs reside in same state
  • substantial portion of events occurred or property located
  • any Δ subject to personal jurisdiction if neither of above applies
π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant.

Venue refers to the federal judicial district where a case may be heard. When a plaintiff sues a federal officer or employee, proper venue depends on whether the defendant is sued in his/her official or individual capacity. When an officer or employee is sued in an official capacity, recovery is sought from the federal government and special venue rules apply. Under one such rule, venue is proper where the plaintiff resides.

In contrast, when an officer or employee is sued in an individual capacity, recovery is sought from the officer or employee. In these suits, the general venue statute applies, and venue is proper only where:

  • any defendant resides, so long as all defendants reside in the same state (residency-based venue)
  • a substantial portion of the events giving rise to the suit occurred (events-based venue) or a substantial part of the property at issue is located (property-based venue) or
  • any defendant is subject to the court's personal jurisdiction, but only if neither of the above provisions applies (fallback provision).

Here, the pedestrian (plaintiff) sued the federal employee (defendant) in State C, where the pedestrian resides. Therefore, venue would only be proper in State C if the employee was sued in his official capacity (Choice C). So, if the court dismisses the action for improper venue, it is likely because the pedestrian sued the employee in his individual capacity.

(Choice B) The employee could have been sued in State A, where he resides. However, he also could have been sued in State B, where the accident giving rise to the suit occurred.

(Choice D) The fact that the suit does not arise under a federal statute relates to subject-matter jurisdiction, not venue. Additionally, subject-matter jurisdiction exists through diversity jurisdiction since the employee and pedestrian are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

📌 Educational Objective

When a federal officer or employee is sued in his/her official capacity, special venue rules apply—eg, venue is proper where the plaintiff resides. However, the general venue statute applies when a federal officer or employee is sued in his/her individual capacity.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1391(e)(1) (proper venue for federal officer or employee sued in official capacity).
  • Stafford v. Briggs, 444 U.S. 527, 542 (1980) (holding that the general venue statute applies when a federal officer or employee is sued in his/her individual capacity).

如果法院批准了该雇员的动议，最可能的解释是什么？

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Jurisdiction & Venue

本题考察的核心是针对联邦雇员（Federal Employee）提起诉讼时，如何确定正确的审判地（Venue）。

核心考点：身份决定规则 审判地的确定取决于被告是被以官方身份（Official Capacity）起诉，还是以个人身份（Individual Capacity）起诉。

1. 两种身份的对比

官方身份 (Official Capacity) 特殊规则

适用情况：原告实际上是在起诉政府，寻求政府行为（如职务令 Mandamus）或政府赔偿。

审判地规则 (28 U.S.C. § 1391(e))：
非常宽松，可以在以下地点起诉：

  • 被告居住地
  • 事件发生地
  • 原告居住地 (Plaintiff's residence) —— 这是关键区别！
个人身份 (Individual Capacity) 一般规则

适用情况：原告寻求被告个人承担赔偿责任（例如本案中的车祸赔偿）。

审判地规则 (28 U.S.C. § 1391(b))：
适用普通民事诉讼的一般规则：

  • 被告居住地（如果所有被告在同一州）
  • 事件发生地
  • 注意：不能在原告居住地起诉。

2. 题目逻辑推演

1
原告的主张：原告在 C 州（原告居住地）起诉，理由是“我是 C 州居民且被告是联邦雇员”。她试图利用针对官方身份的特殊规则 (§ 1391(e))。
2
法院的裁决：法院批准了被告驳回诉讼的动议（Grant Motion to Dismiss）。这意味着法院认为 C 州不是正确的审判地。
3
结论：既然法院拒绝适用“原告居住地”这一规则，说明法院认定本案不属于“官方身份”诉讼，而是“个人身份”诉讼。
判例依据 最高法院在 Stafford v. Briggs (1980) 中明确裁定：旨在向联邦雇员个人寻求金钱赔偿的诉讼，不适用 § 1391(e) 的特殊审判地规则，而应适用一般审判地规则。

3. 为什么选 C？

选项 C (The pedestrian sued the employee in his individual capacity) 是正确答案。

如果原告是以个人身份起诉雇员（要求其个人赔偿车祸损失），则必须适用一般审判地规则。根据一般规则：

  • A 州：被告居住地（可行）
  • B 州：事故发生地（可行）
  • C 州：原告居住地（不可行，除非事件发生在此或被告住在此）

因此，法院驳回 C 州起诉的唯一合理解释是：这是一起个人身份诉讼，不能在原告居住地审理。

4. 其他选项为何错误

  • 选项 A： 法律错误。如果是官方身份诉讼，联邦雇员可以在原告居住地被起诉。
  • 选项 B： 不准确。虽然 A 州（被告居住地）是适当的审判地，但 B 州（事故发生地）也是适当的。题目问的是“解释”，而不是问“哪里是唯一的审判地”。
  • 选项 D： 混淆概念。诉讼是否基于联邦法规涉及的是联邦事项管辖权 (Subject Matter Jurisdiction)，而非审判地 (Venue)。本案基于多元管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction) 已经满足了进联邦法院的门槛。
Exam Tip: 看到“联邦雇员”和“审判地”结合的题目，第一时间判断原告是想要政府赔钱（Official）还是想要雇员个人赔钱（Individual）。如果是个人赔钱，就把它当作普通的民事侵权案处理，不要被“联邦雇员”的身份迷惑。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A bus passenger from State A was injured when a bus owned by a company incorporated and headquartered in State B negligently collided with another vehicle on a road in State A. The passenger agreed to release the company from liability in exchange for a free lifetime bus membership valued at $60,000. Two years later, Congress passed a law that prohibited bus companies from providing free lifetime bus memberships, so the company revoked the passenger's membership.
The passenger sued the company in federal court for breach of contract. In his complaint, the passenger stated that the company would likely argue that its breach was necessary to comply with the federal statute. The passenger claimed that this defense is invalid because the statute violates the U.S. Constitution.
The company filed a motion to dismiss the passenger's suit for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction before filing an answer.
How will the court likely rule on the company's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the company failed to challenge subject-matter jurisdiction in its answer.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the passenger's claim presents a federal issue.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because state courts have exclusive jurisdiction over state-law claims.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction.

questions.explanation:
Well-pleaded complaint rule
(for federal-question jurisdiction)
Federal issue
= element of plaintiff's claim
Federal issue
≠ anticipated defense, counterclaim, answer
United States District Court
for the District of New
York
John Smith, Plaintiff
v.
ABC Co., Defendant
Civil No. 15-CV-XXXXXX
FIRST AMENDED
COMPLAINT

I. Basis for Jurisdiction

  1. Plaintiff asserts that defendant committed trademark infringement in violation of the Lanham Act, 15 U.S.C. § 114.
United States District Court
for the District of New
York
John Smith, Plaintiff
v.
ABC Co., Defendant
Civil No. 15-CV-XXXXXX
DEFENDANT'S
ANSWER AND AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES
United States District Court
for the District of New
York
John Smith, Plaintiff
v.
ABC Co., Defendant
Civil No. 15-CV-XXXXXX
FIRST AMENDED
COMPLAINT

I. Basis for Jurisdiction

  1. Defendant will contend that the state law violates the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution.
United States District Court
for the District of New
York
John Smith, Plaintiff
v.
ABC Co., Defendant
Civil No. 15-CV-XXXXXX
DEFENDANT'S
ANSWER AND AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES

Subject-matter jurisdiction is a court's authority to hear a case on the merits. The party seeking to invoke a federal court's subject-matter jurisdiction (generally the plaintiff) has the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the court has either:

  • diversity jurisdiction — when the parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 (not $60,000, as seen here) or
  • federal-question jurisdiction — when the plaintiff asserts a cause of action that arises under the Constitution, a treaty, or a federal law.

For federal-question jurisdiction to be invoked, the federal issue must appear on the face of the plaintiff's well-pleaded complaint—not the defendant's answer or counterclaim. The jurisdictional statement in the complaint must show that the federal issue is a necessary element of the plaintiff's cause of action.* Merely mentioning a federal issue that may be asserted in the defendant's answer is insufficient.

Here, the passenger's complaint asserts a breach of contract claim. It also states that the company would likely argue that it breached the contract to comply with a federal statute, which the passenger alleges is unconstitutional. Since this federal issue arises from an anticipated defense—not the cause of action—the complaint fails to establish federal-question jurisdiction (Choice B). Therefore, the court will likely grant the company's motion.

*In rare situations, the complete-preemption doctrine allows a state-law claim to be considered a federal-law claim when Congress clearly intended for a federal statute to completely preempt (ie, supersede) state law.

(Choice A) A party or the court can challenge subject-matter jurisdiction at any time, including in a pre-answer motion.

(Choice C) State and federal courts have concurrent (ie, shared) jurisdiction over most state-law claims. The only substantive areas over which state courts have exclusive jurisdiction are probate matters (eg, authenticating a will) and domestic relations (eg, issuing a divorce).

📌 Educational Objective

Federal-question jurisdiction exists when the face of the plaintiff's well-pleaded complaint asserts a claim arising under the Constitution, a federal law, or a treaty. A complaint is well-pleaded when its jurisdictional statement shows that the federal issue is a necessary element of the plaintiff's cause of action.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1331 (federal-question jurisdiction).
  • Louisville & Nashville R.R. Co. v. Mottley, 211 U.S. 149, 152 (1908) (establishing the well-pleaded complaint rule).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 854 (2020) (explaining that anticipated defenses cannot be the basis for federal-question jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
一名来自A州的巴士乘客，因一辆在B州注册成立且总部设在B州的公司所拥有的巴士在A州的道路上因过失与另一辆车相撞而受伤。该乘客同意免除该公司的责任，以换取价值60,000美元的终身免费巴士会员资格。两年后，国会通过了一项法律，禁止巴士公司提供终身免费巴士会员资格，因此该公司撤销了该乘客的会员资格。

该乘客以违约为由在联邦法院起诉该公司。在其诉状中，该乘客陈述，该公司很可能会主张其违约行为是为了遵守联邦法规所必需的。该乘客声称该抗辩无效，因为该法规违反了美国宪法。

在提交答辩状之前，该公司以缺乏标的物管辖权为由，提出了驳回乘客起诉的动议。

法院可能会如何裁定公司的该项动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为公司未在其答辩状中对标的物管辖权提出异议。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为乘客的诉求提出了一个联邦问题。
zh-choices.C: 支持该动议，因为州法院对州法诉求拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.D: 支持该动议，因为法院缺乏标的物管辖权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure · Jurisdiction

本题考察的是联邦法院的标的物管辖权 (Subject-Matter Jurisdiction, SMJ)。正确答案是 D。

要让联邦法院审理此案，原告必须证明法院拥有以下两种管辖权之一：

路径一：多元管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction)

规则：当事人必须是不同州的公民，且争议金额必须超过 $75,000。

本案分析：

  • 当事人：A州 vs B州 ✔ (满足)
  • 金额：$60,000 ✘ (不满足)

结论：因为金额未超过 $75,000，多元管辖权不成立。

路径二：联邦问题管辖权 (Federal Question)

规则：案件必须产生于 (Arise under) 联邦法律、宪法或条约。

核心考点：充分陈述诉状规则 (Well-Pleaded Complaint Rule)

联邦问题必须出现在原告对自己诉求的必要陈述中，而不能仅仅出现在对被告预期抗辩 (Anticipated Defense) 的回应中。

本案分析：原告起诉的是“违约 (Breach of Contract)”，这是州法问题。虽然原告预见到被告会用“联邦法规”作为抗辩，并声称该法规“违宪”，但这只是对辩护的回应，不是诉讼的根基。

结论：联邦问题管辖权不成立。

经典判例回顾

本题的事实模式几乎完全照搬了著名的 Louisville & Nashville R.R. Co. v. Mottley (1908) 案。

在该案中，Mottley 夫妇因受伤获得终身免费火车票，后国会立法禁止。最高法院裁定：原告在诉状中提及被告可能依据联邦法律进行抗辩，这不足以建立联邦管辖权。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
  • 选项 A (错)： 标的物管辖权 (SMJ) 是法院权力的基石，永远不会被放弃 (Waived)。当事人可以在诉讼的任何阶段提出，甚至法院可以自行提出 (Sua Sponte)。
  • 选项 B (错)： 仅仅“涉及”联邦问题是不够的。根据 Mottley 规则，联邦问题必须是原告诉因的必要组成部分。
  • 选项 C (错)： 州法院对大多数联邦诉讼拥有并行管辖权 (Concurrent Jurisdiction)，并非只能审理州法案件。
💡 考试技巧
看到“Anticipated Defense”（预期抗辩）这几个字，立刻警惕 Federal Question Jurisdiction 通常不成立。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An entrepreneur from State A decided to sell hot sauce to the public, labeling it "Best Hot Sauce."
A company incorporated in State B and headquartered in State C sued the entrepreneur in federal court in State C. The complaint sought $50,000 in damages and alleged that the entrepreneur's use of the name "Best Hot Sauce" infringed the company's federal trademark. The entrepreneur filed an answer denying the allegations, and the parties began discovery. Six months later, the entrepreneur moved to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Should the court grant the entrepreneur's motion?

choices.A: No, because the company's claim arises under federal law.
choices.B: No, because the entrepreneur waived the right to challenge subject-matter jurisdiction by not raising the issue initially by motion or in the answer.
choices.C: Yes, because although the claim arises under federal law, the amount in controversy is not satisfied.
choices.D: Yes, because although there is diversity, the amount in controversy is not satisfied.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction
Federal question
Constitution
Federal law
Treaty
OR
Diversity
Diverse citizenship
> $75,000 in controversy

Subject-matter jurisdiction refers to a court's authority to hear a particular type of case or controversy. A federal court* should presume that it lacks subject-matter jurisdiction until the party seeking to invoke the court's jurisdiction (generally the plaintiff) proves that the court has either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – the case arises under the Constitution, a federal law, or a treaty or
  • diversity jurisdiction – the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the parties are citizens of different states.

Here, the company alleges that the entrepreneur infringed upon the company's federal trademark, which involves federal law. As a result, the court has federal-question jurisdiction (and therefore subject-matter jurisdiction) to hear the case. Accordingly, the court should deny the entrepreneur's motion to dismiss.

*Most civil actions invoking federal subject-matter jurisdiction are brought before a federal district court and reviewed by the federal appellate court encompassing that district. However, Congress also created special federal courts with jurisdiction over specific types of cases.

(Choice B) A lack of personal jurisdiction (ie, a court's authority over a defendant) must be raised at the start of a case or it is waived. In contrast, the right to challenge subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived. Instead, this issue can be raised at any time by the parties or on the court's own initiative (ie, sua sponte). As a result, the timing of the entrepreneur's motion challenging subject-matter jurisdiction is immaterial.

(Choice C) Federal-question jurisdiction does not have an amount-in-controversy requirement.

(Choice D) Although the company and the entrepreneur are citizens of different states, the court lacks diversity jurisdiction because the amount in controversy is only $50,000 (less than $75,000). However, the court still has subject-matter jurisdiction because the case involves a federal question.

📌 Educational Objective

Subject-matter jurisdiction exists if there is federal-question jurisdiction—ie, the case arises under the Constitution, a federal law, or a treaty—or diversity jurisdiction—ie, the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the parties are citizens of different states.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1331 (federal-question jurisdiction).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question: 一位来自A州的创业者决定向公众销售辣酱，并将其命名为“Best Hot Sauce”。一家在B州注册成立、总部设在C州的公司，在C州的联邦法院起诉了这位创业者。诉状要求50,000美元的损害赔偿，并声称该创业者使用“Best Hot Sauce”这一名称侵犯了该公司的联邦商标（federal trademark）。创业者提交了答辩状，否认了这些指控，双方开始了证据开示（discovery）。六个月后，创业者动议驳回诉讼，理由是缺乏对案件的属事管辖权（subject-matter jurisdiction）。法院是否应该批准创业者的动议？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该公司的诉求源于联邦法律。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为创业者未能通过动议或在答辩状中初步提出此问题，从而放弃了质疑属事管辖权（subject-matter jurisdiction）的权利。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为尽管诉求源于联邦法律，但争议金额（amount in controversy）未达到要求。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为尽管存在多元化管辖（diversity），但争议金额（amount in controversy）未达到要求。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 属事管辖权

正确答案：A 法院不应批准企业家的动议，因为公司的诉讼请求源于联邦法律。

核心法律规则：联邦法院的属事管辖权

属事管辖权 (Subject-matter jurisdiction, SMJ) 是指法院审理特定类型案件或争议的权力。联邦法院通常推定其不具备属事管辖权，除非主张联邦管辖权的一方能够证明法院具备以下任一条件：

  • 联邦问题管辖权 (Federal-question jurisdiction)：案件源于《宪法》、联邦法律或条约。法定依据为 28 U.S.C. § 1331。
  • 多元化管辖权 (Diversity jurisdiction)：争议金额超过 $75,000 且当事人是不同州的公民。法定依据为 28 U.S.C. § 1332。

*大多数援引联邦属事管辖权的民事诉讼会在联邦地区法院提起，并由该地区的联邦上诉法院审查。然而，国会也设立了对特定类型案件拥有管辖权的特别联邦法院。

概念对比：属事管辖权 vs. 对人管辖权

特征 属事管辖权 (Subject-Matter Jurisdiction) 对人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction)
定义 法院审理特定类型案件的权力。 法院对特定被告行使审判权的权力。
来源 美国宪法第三条、国会立法 (如 28 U.S.C. § 1331, § 1332)。 美国宪法第十四修正案正当程序条款、州长臂法。
可否放弃 不可放弃 (Non-waivable)。当事人或法院可随时提出缺乏属事管辖权。 可放弃 (Waivable)。若未在首次回应（如动议或答辩）中及时提出，则视为放弃。
要求 案件涉及联邦问题，或当事人多元化且争议金额超过 $75,000。 被告与法院地州有“最低联系”，且行使管辖权符合“公平正义和实质性正当程序”。

案情分析与逻辑推理

1. 确定诉讼请求性质： 本案中，公司起诉企业家侵犯其联邦商标权。联邦商标法是联邦法律。

2. 评估联邦问题管辖权： 根据联邦问题管辖权的定义，如果案件源于联邦法律，联邦法院就具备审理该案件的属事管辖权。由于公司的主张明确涉及联邦商标法，因此联邦法院具备联邦问题管辖权来审理此案。

3. 评估多元化管辖权：

  • 公民身份： 企业家来自州A，公司注册在州B且总部在州C。当事人是不同州的公民，满足多元化管辖权的公民身份要求。
  • 争议金额： 争议金额为 $50,000。这未达到多元化管辖权要求的 $75,000 门槛。因此，本案不具备多元化管辖权。

4. 结论： 尽管不具备多元化管辖权，但由于存在联邦问题管辖权，联邦法院仍有权审理此案。联邦问题管辖权没有争议金额要求。因此，法院应驳回企业家提出的缺乏属事管辖权的动议。

核心概念图示

联邦法院的属事管辖权 (Subject-Matter Jurisdiction)

联邦问题管辖权 (Federal Question)

宪法 (Constitution) 联邦法律 (Federal Law) 条约 (Treaty)
或 (OR)

多元化管辖权 (Diversity)

不同州公民身份 (Diverse Citizenship) 争议金额 > $75,000 (Amount in Controversy > $75,000)

MBE 考点陷阱

常见误区与提示

陷阱： 许多考生会混淆属事管辖权和对人管辖权的可放弃性。属事管辖权是联邦法院的固有权力，不能通过当事人同意或未及时提出异议而获得或放弃。法院甚至可以主动 (sua sponte) 提出缺乏属事管辖权。

提示： 联邦问题管辖权没有争议金额要求，而多元化管辖权则有严格的 $75,000 门槛。在分析时，务必先检查是否存在联邦问题，再考虑多元化管辖权。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 不应批准，因为公司的诉讼请求源于联邦法律。

正确。 公司起诉侵犯联邦商标权，这直接涉及联邦法律，因此联邦法院拥有联邦问题管辖权。联邦问题管辖权没有争议金额要求，所以争议金额为 $50,000 并不影响联邦法院的属事管辖权。

B. 不应批准，因为企业家未能在最初通过动议或答辩提出异议，从而放弃了挑战属事管辖权的权利。

错误。 属事管辖权是不可放弃的，可以在诉讼的任何阶段提出，甚至由法院主动提出。这与对人管辖权不同，对人管辖权若未及时提出则可能被视为放弃。

C. 应批准，因为尽管诉讼请求源于联邦法律，但争议金额不满足要求。

错误。 尽管案件源于联邦法律，但联邦问题管辖权没有争议金额要求。只有多元化管辖权才要求争议金额超过 $75,000。因此，争议金额不影响联邦问题管辖权的存在。

D. 应批准，因为尽管存在多元化，但争议金额不满足要求。

错误。 尽管当事人是不同州的公民（企业家来自州A，公司注册在州B，总部在州C，满足多元化管辖权的公民身份要求），但争议金额为 $50,000，未达到多元化管辖权要求的 $75,000。因此，本案不具备多元化管辖权。然而，由于存在联邦问题，法院仍有属事管辖权，所以动议不应被批准。

MBE 考试技巧

记住联邦法院的两种主要属事管辖权：联邦问题管辖权 (案件源于联邦法律、宪法或条约，无金额要求) 和 多元化管辖权 (当事人是不同州的公民 且 争议金额 > $75,000)。最重要的是，属事管辖权永远不能被放弃，可以在诉讼的任何阶段提出。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A farmer from State A purchased farmland from a woman who lives in State B. Prior to the purchase, a private land inspector from State B tested the soil and concluded that it was adequate for farming operations. Upon taking possession of the land, however, the farmer realized that the woman had polluted the soil to such an extent that he could not maintain farming operations.
The farmer sued the woman in federal court under a federal environmental statute for $300,000. The farmer also joined the inspector to this suit to recover $50,000 for the inspector's negligent inspection of the land.
The inspector filed a motion to dismiss the farmer's claim against him for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
How will the court likely rule on the inspector's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because although there is no federal-question or diversity jurisdiction over the farmer's claim against the inspector, there is supplemental jurisdiction over this claim.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because there is federal-question jurisdiction over the farmer's claim against the inspector.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because a federal court can never hear a claim over which it does not have federal-question or diversity jurisdiction.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because there is no federal-question, diversity, or supplemental jurisdiction over the farmer's claim against the inspector.

questions.explanation:
Subject-matter jurisdiction
Original jurisdiction
  • Federal question – claim arises under U.S. Constitution, treaty, or federal law or
  • Diversity – opponents are citizens of different states & amount in controversy > $75,000
—Yes → Subject-matter jurisdiction
No
↓
Supplemental
Claim shares common nucleus of operative facts as claim within court's original jurisdiction
— No → No subject-matter jurisdiction
Yes
↓
Original claim based solely on diversity jurisdiction
Supplemental claim:
  • permissive joinder by plaintiff would destroy complete diversity or
  • made by existing plaintiffs:
    against joined, intervening, or impleaded parties or
    seeking compulsory joinder or intervention
Yes
↓
No subject-matter jurisdiction
Court may decline jurisdiction if:
  • claim raises novel/complex issue of state law
  • claim predominates over original claims
  • original claims have been dismissed or
  • other compelling reason
No

Subject-matter jurisdiction refers to a federal court's authority to hear a type of dispute. This requirement is met when a dispute falls within either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – the dispute arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or a federal law or
  • diversity jurisdiction – the opposing parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy for each claim exceeds $75,000.

Here, federal-question jurisdiction exists over the farmer's claim against the woman because it arises under the federal statute. But such jurisdiction does not exist over his state law negligence claim against the inspector (Choice B). And though the opposing parties reside in different states (States A and B), the federal court lacks diversity jurisdiction over this claim since the amount in controversy is merely $50,000.

When only some claims in a dispute fall within the court's original subject-matter jurisdiction (as seen here), the court can exercise supplemental jurisdiction to hear the remaining claims in some instances (Choice C). This is permitted when a supplemental claim shares a common nucleus of operative facts with a claim within the court's original subject-matter jurisdiction. But if the original claim is based on federal-question jurisdiction, the court can decline to exercise supplemental jurisdiction for any of the following discretionary reasons:

  • the supplemental claim raises a novel/complex state law issue
  • the supplemental claim predominates over the original claims
  • the original claims have been dismissed or
  • another compelling reason exists.

(Choice A) Here, the farmer's claims share a common nucleus of operative facts because they arise from the same polluted soil. And since the farmer's claim against the woman is based on federal-question jurisdiction—and none of the discretionary reasons apply—the court may exercise supplemental jurisdiction over his claim against the inspector. As a result, the court will likely deny the inspector's motion to dismiss (Choice D).

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court will generally exercise supplemental jurisdiction over a claim that falls outside of its original subject-matter jurisdiction if it shares a common nucleus of operative facts with a claim that arises under federal-question jurisdiction—unless it declines to do so for a discretionary reason.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1367 (supplemental jurisdiction).
  • Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Allapattah Servs., 545 U.S. 546, 557–60 (2005) (explaining supplemental jurisdiction).

一名来自A州的农民从一名居住在B州的女性处购买了农田。在购买之前，一名来自B州的私人土地检验员对土壤进行了检测，并得出结论认为该土壤适合耕作。然而，在占有该土地后，农民发现该女性对土壤的污染程度已经严重到他无法维持耕作的程度。

法院很可能会如何裁决检验员的动议？

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Jurisdiction

本题考察的核心是联邦法院的补充管辖权 (Supplemental Jurisdiction)。正确答案是 A。

核心法律规则：28 U.S.C. § 1367
如果联邦法院对某个案件拥有“初始管辖权”（如联邦问题管辖权），那么法院也有权审理与该案件具有“共同案件事实核心” (Common Nucleus of Operative Fact) 的其他相关州法诉求。

第一步：分析“锚定”诉求 (The Anchor Claim)

农民起诉女性（被告1）是基于联邦环境法规。这赋予了联邦法院联邦问题管辖权 (Federal Question Jurisdiction)。

这是一个稳固的“锚”，使得案件可以进入联邦法院。

第二步：分析“附加”诉求 (The Supplemental Claim)

农民起诉检验员（被告2）是基于疏忽（Negligence），这是州法问题，不是联邦问题。

虽然双方来自不同州（A州 vs B州），但索赔金额仅为 $50,000，未达到多元管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction) 要求的 $75,000 门槛。

因此，该诉求本身没有独立的进入联邦法院的资格。

第三步：应用补充管辖权

根据 United Mine Workers v. Gibbs 确立的原则及 § 1367(a)：

  • 农民对检验员的诉求与对女性的诉求是否源于同一事实？
    是的。 两者都源于同一块受污染的土地交易。
  • 它们共享“共同的案件事实核心”吗？
    是的。

因此，联邦法院可以行使补充管辖权将检验员留在案中，即使针对他的索赔金额不足。

MBE 陷阱提示 (Exam Tip)

考生常混淆 § 1367(b) 的限制。请注意：

如果初始案件仅基于多元管辖权进入联邦法院，那么原告根据 Rule 14, 19, 20, 24 加入被告时，通常不能使用补充管辖权来规避多元性的要求。

但是！本题的初始案件是基于联邦问题 (Federal Question)。在这种情况下，§ 1367(b) 的限制不适用。只要满足事实关联性，法院通常会行使管辖权。

结论：法院将驳回检验员的动议 (Deny the motion)。
虽然没有独立的管辖权，但存在补充管辖权。
