questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman sued her former employer in state court, asserting age and sex discrimination claims under both state and federal law. The woman's attorney had recently been embarrassed in court by the judge to whom the case was assigned. Wishing to avoid difficulties with the judge, the woman's attorney promptly removed the case to federal court on the basis of federal-question jurisdiction. The employer's attorney has timely moved to remand.
How is the federal court likely to proceed?

choices.A: Remand the entire case.
choices.B: Remand the state claims but keep the federal claims.
choices.C: Retain the case, because it was timely removed and the woman alleges federal claims.
choices.D: Retain the case to avoid the risk of bias and impropriety in having it proceed before a judge who has shown clear hostility toward the woman's attorney.

questions.explanation:
Remand based on improper removal
Basis Example Result
No subject-matter jurisdiction • No subject-matter jurisdiction over any claim • Remand entire case
• No subject-matter jurisdiction over some claims • Retain removable claims
• Sever & remand nonremovable claims
Procedural error • Defendant filed notice of removal more than 30 days after receiving complaint
• Not all defendants consented to removal
• Case removed by plaintiff (not defendant)
• Notice not delivered to parties or state court
• Removal violates forum-defendant rule 		• Remand entire case

A defendant can remove a case originally filed in state court to federal court if:

• the federal court has subject-matter jurisdiction over the plaintiff's claims—eg, when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law

• all defendants consent to removal

• the defendant files a notice of removal within 30 days of receiving the plaintiff's initial complaint or service of the summons (whichever period is shorter) and

• a copy of the notice of removal is delivered to the state court and the other parties.

A party can challenge removal by filing a motion to remand (ie, return) the case to state court. This motion must generally be filed in federal court within 30 days after the notice of removal is filed, but a motion based on lack of subject-matter jurisdiction can be filed at any time. The burden is then on the party seeking removal to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that removal is proper. If there was a procedural error in the removal, the federal court should remand the entire case to state court.*

Here, the woman sued her former employer in state court, and her attorney promptly removed the case to federal court. However, there was a procedural error in that removal since the woman is the plaintiff—not the defendant. Therefore, the federal court will likely remand the entire case.

*The federal court clerk must mail a certified copy of the remand order to the state court clerk. The order may require payment of costs, including attorney's fees. But if a remand is based on procedural error (as in this case), attorney's fees can only be awarded if there was no objectively reasonable basis for removal.

(Choice B) Had the federal court lacked subject-matter jurisdiction over some of the woman's claims (eg, her state claims), it would have remanded those claims but kept the removable claims (eg, her federal claims).

(Choice C) Although the case may have been timely removed and the woman alleges federal claims, removal is improper because she is the plaintiff.

(Choice D) A plaintiff cannot remove a case, even if there is a risk of bias and impropriety in having the case proceed before a hostile state-court judge.

📌 Educational Objective

If a procedural error occurs in the removal of a case from state to federal court (eg, removal by the plaintiff), the federal court should remand the entire case.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. §§ 1441, 1446 (removal of civil actions).

联邦法院可能会如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 将整个案件发回重审。
zh-choices.B: 将州法诉求发回重审，但保留联邦法诉求。
zh-choices.C: 保留该案件，因为移送及时且该女性主张了联邦法诉求。
zh-choices.D: 保留该案件，以避免在对该女性律师表现出明显敌意的法官面前审理所带来的偏见和不当风险。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure (民事诉讼法)
正确答案：A
Remand the entire case
(将整个案件发回重审)
核心考点：移送管辖权 (Removal Jurisdiction)

本题考察的是谁有权将案件从州法院移送至联邦法院。

黄金法则：
根据 28 U.S.C. § 1441，只有被告 (Defendant) 有权寻求移送 (Removal)。

❌ 原告 (Plaintiff) 永远不能移送案件，即使原告在起诉后提出了联邦法诉求，或者面临州法院的反诉。
本案分析
1
谁发起了移送？
题目中明确指出是“该女性的律师” (The woman's attorney) 移送了案件。该女性是原告 (Plaintiff)。
2
是否存在程序错误？
是的。原告移送案件属于严重的程序错误 (Procedural Defect)。
3
法院如何处理？
由于被告及时提出了发回重审动议 (Motion to Remand)，联邦法院必须批准该动议，将整个案件退回州法院。
为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 B (部分发回)： 只有在移送本身是合法的（即由被告发起），但某些诉求缺乏联邦管辖权时，才会考虑分离诉求。本案中移送主体错误，整个移送无效。
  • 选项 C (保留案件)： 即使案件涉及联邦问题 (Federal Question)，也不赋予原告移送权。原告既然选择了州法院作为起诉地 (Forum)，就必须受其约束。
  • 选项 D (因偏见保留)： 偏见 (Bias) 不是移送的理由。
    如果州法官有偏见，原告的正确救济途径是在州法院申请法官回避 (Recusal)，而不是移送至联邦法院。
💡 MBE 拿分技巧：
看到 "Removal" (移送) 题目时，第一步先检查是谁在移送。
如果是 Plaintiff，直接选 "Remand" (发回重审)。不要被题目中提到的“联邦问题”、“多元管辖权”或“法官偏见”所迷惑，这些都是干扰信息。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An artist living in State A entered into a contract with a gallery from State A that allowed the gallery to display and sell the artist's paintings, with the artist to receive a commission for any paintings sold. Shortly thereafter, the artist moved to State B, where he joined a local artists' collective. The gallery sold several of the artist's paintings but refused to provide the commission the artist thought he was due under the contract. The artist sued the gallery in a federal court in State A for breach of contract and requested $100,000 in damages. The day after filing his complaint, the artist moved back to State A, claiming artistic differences with the artists' collective.
The gallery filed an answer that did not include a defense of a lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. The gallery then moved to dismiss the artist's complaint for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
How will the federal court most likely rule on the gallery's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the gallery waived its subject-matter jurisdiction defense by failing to include it in its answer.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because there is diversity of citizenship and the amount in controversy is $100,000.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because both parties are citizens of State A.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because state courts have exclusive jurisdiction over state-law claims.

questions.explanation:
Determining diversity of citizenship
Contract formed
Artist – State A
Gallery – State A
Alleged breach
occurred
Artist – State B
Gallery – State A
Citizenship determined
Complaint filed in
federal court

Artist – State B
Gallery – State A
Case proceeds
Artist – State A
Gallery – State A

A federal court can only hear the merits of a lawsuit if the court has subject-matter jurisdiction, which can arise under:

• federal-question jurisdiction – when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or

• diversity jurisdiction – when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states (ie, are diverse).

Citizenship is determined on the date that the plaintiff's complaint is filed with the court.

Here, the artist's breach-of-contract suit against the gallery for $100,000 in damages satisfies the amount-in-controversy requirement. And though both parties were State A citizens when they entered the contract and are currently State A citizens, the artist was a State B citizen when he filed the complaint. As a result, the parties were diverse when the filing occurred—satisfying the requirements for diversity jurisdiction (Choice C). The federal court therefore has subject-matter jurisdiction to hear this suit and will likely deny the gallery's motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) Most defenses are waived if they are not asserted in a defendant's answer. But a defense based on lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived and can be asserted by a party or raised by the court at any time—including after an answer has been filed.

(Choice D) State and federal courts have concurrent (ie, shared) jurisdiction over most state-law claims. The only substantive areas over which state courts have exclusive jurisdiction are probate matters (eg, authenticating a will) and domestic relations (eg, issuing a divorce).

📌 Educational Objective

Subject-matter jurisdiction arises under diversity jurisdiction when (1) the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and (2) the opposing parties are citizens of different states on the date the complaint is filed.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (requirements for diversity jurisdiction).
  • Grupo Dataflux v. Atlas Global Group, Ltd. P'ship, 541 U.S. 567, 570–71 (2004) (holding that the citizenship of the parties in a lawsuit is determined at the time the suit is filed).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法 (Civil Procedure)

本题考察的核心知识点是联邦法院的州籍多元化管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction) 及其判定的时间节点。

⚖️ 黄金法则：起诉时原则 (Time-of-Filing Rule)

根据 28 U.S.C. § 1332 和最高法院判例（如 Grupo Dataflux v. Atlas Global Group），当事人的公民身份（Citizenship）仅在诉状提交之日 (Date the complaint is filed) 确定。

此后的住所变更不影响已经确立的管辖权。

📅 案情时间线分析

合同签订时
原告：A州 | 被告：A州
(此时无多元化，但不重要)
🚨 提交诉状时 (关键时刻)
原告：B州 | 被告：A州
✅ 满足完全多元化 (Complete Diversity)
起诉后第二天
原告搬回 A州
(根据规则，这一变化被忽略)

🔍 选项深度解析

选项 B (正确)

理由：联邦法院拥有管辖权，因为：

  1. 争议金额：$100,000 > $75,000 法定门槛。
  2. 州籍多元：在起诉的那一刻，原告是B州公民，被告是A州公民。

法院将驳回被告的动议（Deny the motion），因为管辖权已经有效建立。

选项 A (错误)

陷阱点：管辖权抗辩的放弃。
虽然大多数抗辩（如缺乏对人管辖权 Personal Jurisdiction）若未在答辩状中提出即视为放弃，但缺乏标的物管辖权 (Subject-Matter Jurisdiction, SMJ) 是永远不会被放弃 (Never Waived) 的。被告可以在诉讼的任何阶段提出，甚至法院也可以依职权 (Sua Sponte) 提出。

选项 C (错误)

错误逻辑：此选项错误地依据了“当前”或“起诉后”的公民身份。只要起诉那一刻是多元的，后续搬回A州不会破坏管辖权。

选项 D (错误)

错误逻辑：专属管辖权。
州法院对州法诉求（如违约）确实有管辖权，但这通常是并行管辖权 (Concurrent Jurisdiction)，而非专属管辖权。只要满足多元化条件，联邦法院完全可以审理州法合同纠纷。

🎓 MBE 提分技巧：

看到题目中出现当事人“搬家” (Moving) 的情节，立即警觉：
  1. 检查搬家是在起诉前还是起诉后。
  2. 如果是起诉前搬家，检查是否有意图定居（改变了州籍）。
  3. 如果是起诉后搬家（如本题），直接忽略该变化！它旨在干扰你的判断。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An airline incorporated and with its principal place of business in State A contracted with a manufacturer incorporated and headquartered in State B to buy a new series of planes. The manufacturer bought the planes' engines from a company incorporated and with its principal place of business in State C. The manufacturer delivered the planes to the airline. After six months, all of the planes' engines failed.
The airline filed a complaint against the manufacturer and the company in a state court in State A for breach of contract, seeking $500 million in damages. The manufacturer and the company were served with process, and the company immediately filed a notice of removal. The manufacturer filed a motion to remand.
Will the federal court likely grant the manufacturer's motion to remand?

choices.A: No, because due process requires that a federal court hear cases involving diverse parties.
choices.B: No, because the parties are diverse and the amount in controversy is $500 million.
choices.C: Yes, because the airline is based in State A.
choices.D: Yes, because the manufacturer did not consent to removal.

questions.explanation:
Requirements for removal to federal court
Federal court has original jurisdiction over π’s claims
Federal question
Arises under U.S. Constitution, treaty, or federal law
Diversity
Amount in controversy >$75,000 & diversity of citizenship
No Δ is citizen of state where case was originally filed
All Δs consent to removal
Notice filed in federal court within 30 days of initial complaint or summons; copy delivered to parties & state court
π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant

A plaintiff can choose to file suit in state or federal court. However, a defendant may remove a suit filed in state court to federal court if the case falls within the federal court's subject-matter jurisdiction. This can arise from either:

  • federal-question jurisdiction — when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (not seen here) or
  • diversity jurisdiction — when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states.

A defendant must file a notice of removal in federal court within 30 days after receipt of the initial complaint or service of the summons—whichever period is shorter.* The defendant must also obtain the consent of all other defendants to the removal. If these requirements are not met or some other procedural error occurs, the federal court should grant a motion to remand (ie, return) the entire case to state court.

Here, diversity jurisdiction exists because the airline from State A sued the manufacturer from State B and the company from State C for $500 million in damages. The company timely filed a notice of removal after being served with process but failed to obtain the manufacturer's consent to the removal. As a result, removal is improper, and the federal court will likely grant the manufacturer's motion to remand (Choice B).

*If a suit later becomes removable based on an amended pleading or motion, notice must be filed within 30 days of receipt of the amended pleading or motion. But if more than one year has passed since the suit was commenced and removal is based on diversity jurisdiction, then the suit can only be removed if the plaintiff acted in bad faith.

(Choice A) Due process does not require that federal courts hear cases involving diverse parties. State courts may also hear such cases unless Congress grants federal courts exclusive jurisdiction (not seen here).

(Choice C) The fact that the airline (plaintiff) is from State A does not provide a basis to remand the case. The home-court advantage (ie, forum-defendant) rule prohibits removal in a diversity case when a defendant is a citizen of the state in which the case was filed.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant must obtain the consent of all the other defendants to remove the suit from state to federal court.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1441 (removal requirements).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b)(2)(A) (consent requirement for removal).

一家在A州注册成立且主营业地在A州的航空公司，与一家在B州注册成立且总部位于B州的制造商签订了购买一个新系列飞机的合同。该制造商从一家在C州注册成立且主营业地在C州的公司购买了飞机的发动机。制造商向航空公司交付了飞机。六个月后，所有飞机的发动机均发生故障。

该航空公司以违约为由，在A州的州法院对制造商和发动机公司提起诉讼，要求赔偿5亿美元。制造商和该公司均收到了诉讼文书送达，发动机公司立即提交了移送申请。制造商提出了发回原审法院的动议。

联邦法院是否可能批准制造商的发回动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为正当程序要求联邦法院审理涉及不同州当事人的案件。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为各方当事人来自不同州，且争议金额为5亿美元。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为航空公司位于A州。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为制造商不同意移送。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：民事诉讼法
正确答案：D

核心考点：一致同意规则

本题考察的是案件从州法院移送至联邦法院（Removal）时的程序要求，特别是一致同意规则 (Rule of Unanimity)。

虽然本案满足联邦法院的多元管辖权 (Diversity Jurisdiction)，但由于其中一名被告（制造商）反对移送，导致移送程序有瑕疵，因此联邦法院必须将案件发回 (Remand) 州法院。

法律依据与推理

28 U.S.C. § 1446(b)(2)(A)
当民事诉讼是基于多元管辖权被移送时，所有已收到送达的被告必须都同意或加入该移送申请。

案情分析：

被告 A
(发动机公司)
✅ 申请移送
+
被告 B
(制造商)
❌ 反对移送
=
🚫
移送失败
  • 管辖权基础： 原告（A州）起诉被告（B州和C州），金额$5亿。这确实满足多元管辖权（完全多元 + 超过$75k）。
  • 程序障碍： 尽管联邦法院可以审理此案，但移送（Removal）是一项被告的特权。法律规定，如果有多个被告，必须全员一致同意才能把案件从州法院“搬”到联邦法院。
  • 结果： 制造商提交了发回动议（Motion to Remand），明确表示不同意移送。因此，联邦法院必须批准该动议。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 A (正当程序)：
错误。正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 并不强制要求联邦法院审理多元案件。州法院完全有资格审理涉及外州当事人的案件（拥有一般管辖权）。

❌ 选项 B (多元管辖权存在)：
这是最强的干扰项。虽然案件实质上符合联邦管辖条件（Diversity + Amount in Controversy），但程序上必须满足所有被告同意的要求。仅有管辖权是不够的，程序必须合法。

❌ 选项 C (原告所在地)：
错误。原告是A州公民这一事实本身不影响移送。
注意： 如果被告是A州公民（法院地被告规则 Forum Defendant Rule），那么确实不能移送。但这里原告的国籍不构成发回理由。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Removal (移送) 问题时，请按以下步骤检查：

  1. Subject Matter Jurisdiction: 是否有联邦管辖权（联邦问题或多元管辖）？
  2. Forum Defendant Rule: 如果是多元管辖案件，是否有任何被告是“本州人”（即在州法院所在州）？如果是，不能移送。
  3. Rule of Unanimity: 是否所有被送达的被告都同意移送？只要有一人反对，就不能移送。

本题考查的就是第3点。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
The driver of a compact car from State A that was broadsided by a sedan filed an action in the federal district court for the Middle District of State B. Named as defendants in the complaint were the driver of the sedan, who is a resident of the Eastern District of State B, the passenger in the sedan, who is a resident of the Middle District of State B, and the owner of a bar who, on the evening of the accident, had served alcohol to the occupants of the sedan. The owner of the bar is a resident of the Western District of State B, where the accident occurred.
Can the driver of the sedan successfully challenge the venue of this action as improper?

choices.A: No, because all defendants are residents of State B and the sedan's passenger is a resident of the Middle District.
choices.B: No, because the other defendants have not joined in the challenge.
choices.C: Yes, because a more convenient venue is available.
choices.D: Yes, because the bar owner resides in the district in which the accident occurred and venue is proper only in that district.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Venue
Proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1391) 		Case may be brought in any federal district where:
• any defendant resides, if defendants all reside in same state
• substantial part of events giving rise to claim occurred or property at issue is located
• any defendant is subject to court's personal jurisdiction (if neither of the above provisions applies)
Transfer from proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1404) 		When venue is proper, district court may transfer case to any other proper venue for convenience of parties/witnesses & in interest of justice
Transfer or dismissal from improper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1406) 		When venue is improper, district court must either:
• dismiss case
• transfer case to proper venue (if interest of justice requires)

In general, venue in a federal civil action is proper in any judicial district in which:

• any defendant resides, so long as all defendants reside in the same state or
• a substantial part of the events or omissions on which the claim is based occurred or a substantial part of the property that is the subject of the action is located.*

Here, all three defendants reside in State B. And one of the defendants—the sedan's passenger—is a resident of the Middle District of State B. As a result, venue is proper in this district. Accordingly, the driver of the sedan cannot successfully challenge venue as improper.

*If venue cannot be established in any judicial district based on the residency of the defendants or based on the events or property at issue, then venue is proper in any judicial district in which any defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction.

(Choice B) Any defendant may raise the issue of improper venue without the rest of the defendants joining in that challenge.

(Choice C) Federal district courts may transfer cases to other federal district courts for the convenience of the parties. But even though another venue might be more convenient for the driver of the sedan or the owner of the bar, it does not change the fact that venue is proper in the Middle District of State B.

(Choice D) Venue can be proper in multiple judicial districts. And here, venue would also be proper in the Western District of State B—where the bar owner resides and the accident occurred. But venue is still proper in the Middle District of State B because the passenger resides there and all defendants reside in State B.

📌 Educational Objective

Venue is proper in any judicial district in which (1) any defendant resides, if all defendants reside in the same state or (2) a substantial part of the events on which the claim is based occurred or a substantial part of the property at issue is located.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C § 1391 (providing rules for proper venue).
questions.zh-question:
一辆来自A州的紧凑型轿车被一辆轿车侧面撞击后，其司机在B州中区联邦地区法院提起诉讼。诉状中列为被告的有：轿车司机（B州东区居民）、轿车乘客（B州中区居民），以及一家酒吧的老板（B州西区居民，事故发生地），该老板在事故当晚曾向轿车乘员提供酒精饮品。
轿车司机能否成功质疑本诉讼的审判地（venue）不当？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为所有被告都是B州居民，且轿车乘客是中区居民。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为其他被告尚未加入质疑。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为有一个更方便的审判地（venue）可用。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为酒吧老板居住在事故发生的区域，且审判地（venue）仅在该区域是适当的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 管辖与审判地

正确答案是 A。

由于所有被告都居住在同一州（B州），且其中一名被告居住在B州中区，因此B州中区是适当的审判地。

核心法律规则

联邦法院的审判地 (Venue)

根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391，在联邦民事诉讼中，venue (审判地) 在以下任一 judicial district (司法区) 是适当的：

  1. 任何 defendant (被告) resides (居住) 的司法区，前提是所有被告都居住在同一州；或
  2. 引起诉讼的事件或遗漏的实质部分发生地，或诉讼标的财产的实质部分所在地；或
  3. 如果以上两种情况都无法确定审判地，则为任何被告受 personal jurisdiction (个人管辖) 的司法区。

如果审判地不适当，法院必须驳回案件或将其移送至适当的审判地（如果司法利益要求）。

概念对比

概念 描述
适当的审判地 (Proper Venue)
(28 U.S.C. § 1391)		 案件可以在以下联邦司法区提起：
  • 任何被告居住的司法区，如果所有被告都居住在同一州；
  • 引起诉讼的事件或遗漏的实质部分发生地，或诉讼标的财产的实质部分所在地；
  • 任何被告受法院个人管辖的司法区（如果上述两者都不适用）。
从适当审判地移送 (Transfer from Proper Venue)
(28 U.S.C. § 1404)		 当审判地适当，地区法院可以为了当事人/证人的便利和司法利益，将案件移送至任何其他适当的审判地。
从不适当审判地移送或驳回 (Transfer or Dismissal from Improper Venue)
(28 U.S.C. § 1406)		 当审判地不适当，地区法院必须：
  • 驳回案件；或
  • 将案件移送至适当的审判地（如果司法利益要求）。

案件事实与适用逻辑

1. 识别当事人及其居住地

  • 原告（紧凑型轿车司机）：A州居民。
  • 被告1（轿车司机）：B州东区居民。
  • 被告2（轿车乘客）：B州中区居民。
  • 被告3（酒吧老板）：B州西区居民。事故发生在B州西区。

2. 评估审判地规则 § 1391(b)(1)

根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1)，如果所有被告都居住在同一州，则审判地在任何被告居住的司法区是适当的。

  • 本案中，所有三名被告（轿车司机、轿车乘客、酒吧老板）都居住在B州。
  • 被告之一（轿车乘客）居住在B州中区。

因此，B州中区是适当的审判地。

3. 结论

由于B州中区是适当的审判地，轿车司机（被告）不能成功地以审判地不适当为由提出异议。

案件当事人与审判地关系

原告 (A州)
→
联邦地区法院 (B州中区)
被告居住地：
轿车司机 (B州东区)
轿车乘客 (B州中区)
酒吧老板 (B州西区)

所有被告均居住在B州，且轿车乘客居住在B州中区，故B州中区为适当审判地。

考点陷阱提示

审判地可能在多个司法区适当： MBE 考试中一个常见的陷阱是假设只有一个“最”适当的审判地。实际上，根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391 的规定，审判地可能在多个司法区都是适当的。只要满足任一条件，该司法区就是适当的审判地，即使存在其他更“方便”或与案件联系更紧密的司法区。

便利性与审判地适当性： 审判地的“便利性”是法院考虑是否将案件从一个适当的审判地移送（根据 § 1404）的因素，而不是判断审判地是否适当（根据 § 1391）的因素。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 否，因为所有被告都是B州居民，且轿车乘客是中区居民。

正确。根据 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1)，如果所有被告都居住在同一州，则审判地在任何被告居住的司法区是适当的。本案中，所有被告都居住在B州，且轿车乘客居住在B州中区。因此，B州中区是适当的审判地，轿车司机不能成功地以审判地不适当为由提出异议。

B. 否，因为其他被告没有加入异议。

错误。任何被告都可以单独提出审判地不适当的异议，无需其他被告加入。然而，本案中审判地是适当的，所以异议本身就会失败。

C. 是，因为有更方便的审判地。

错误。审判地的“便利性”是法院考虑是否将案件从一个适当的审判地移送（根据 § 1404）的因素，而不是判断审判地是否适当（根据 § 1391）的因素。即使存在更方便的审判地，也不能使当前适当的审判地变得不适当。

D. 是，因为酒吧老板居住在事故发生的地区，且审判地只在该地区适当。

错误。审判地可能在多个司法区都是适当的。虽然B州西区（酒吧老板居住地和事故发生地）也可能是适当的审判地，但这并不意味着B州中区（轿车乘客居住地）就不适当。只要满足 § 1391 的任一条件，审判地就是适当的。

考点速记

审判地规则 (Venue Rules) 核心：

  1. 被告居住地：所有被告同州，则任何被告居住地均可。
  2. 事件发生地：案件事件或财产所在地。
  3. 兜底条款：若前两者不适用，则任何被告受个人管辖的地区。

记住，审判地可以有多个适当的地点，便利性是移送的理由，而非判断适当性的标准。

参考文献

参考：28 U.S.C. § 1391 (提供适当审判地规则)

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A corporation that owns and operates a helicopter provides transportation for businesspersons within a large metropolitan area that includes the Eastern District of State A and the Western District of State B. The widow of a passenger who was killed when the helicopter crashed in the Eastern District of State A brought a wrongful death action against the corporation in the federal district court for the Western District of State A. The corporation was incorporated in State B and has its principal place of business in State C. The corporation did not file a pre-answer motion to dismiss. In its answer, the corporation alleged that venue was improper and sought an order dismissing the action.
If the court determines that it is in the interest of justice, may the court transfer the action to the Eastern District of State A?

choices.A: No, because the corporation failed to file a motion to dismiss before its answer.
choices.B: No, because the court must dismiss the action if it determines that venue is improper.
choices.C: Yes, because the court on its own initiative may transfer an action from one proper venue to another proper venue.
choices.D: Yes, because venue is proper in the Eastern District of State A.

questions.explanation:
Venue
Proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1391)		 Case may be brought in any federal district where:
  • any defendant resides, if defendants all reside in same state
  • substantial part of events giving rise to claim occurred or property at issue is located
  • any defendant is subject to court's personal jurisdiction (if neither of the above provisions applies)
Transfer from proper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1404)		 When venue is proper, district court may transfer case to any other proper venue for convenience of parties/witnesses & in interest of justice
Transfer or dismissal from improper venue
(28 U.S.C. § 1406)		 When venue is improper, district court must either:
  • dismiss case
  • transfer case to proper venue (if interest of justice requires)

In general, venue in a federal civil action is proper in a judicial district in which:

  • any defendant resides, if all defendants reside in the state in which the district is located or
  • a substantial part of the events or omissions that gave rise to the suit occurred or the property at issue is located.*

For venue purposes, a business entity (e.g., corporation) is a resident of any judicial district where it is subject to personal jurisdiction—e.g., where it is incorporated and/or maintains its principal place of business.

Here, the corporation (business entity) resides in State B (state of incorporation) and State C (principal place of business)—not the Western District of State A. Additionally, the helicopter crash (event giving rise to suit) occurred in the Eastern District of State A. And there is no indication that the corporation has any contact with the Western District of State A. Consequently, venue is improper in the Western District of State A.

When venue is improper, a federal court must either (1) dismiss the case or (2) transfer the case to a federal court with proper venue if doing so would be in the interest of justice (Choice B). Here, venue would be proper in the Eastern District of State A because the helicopter crash occurred there and the corporation is incorporated there. Therefore, if the court determines that it is in the interest of justice, it may transfer the case to that district.

*If venue cannot be established based on residence, events, or property, it can be established based on where the defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction.

(Choice A) A defendant waives an improper-venue defense if it is not asserted in a pre-answer motion or answer—whichever occurs first. Here, the corporation did not waive this defense because it was asserted in the answer and no pre-answer motion had been filed.

(Choice B) Venue was improper in the Western District of State A. Accordingly, the rules governing improper venue control here.

📌 Educational Objective

When venue is improper, the court must (1) dismiss the case or (2) transfer the case to a district with proper venue if it would be in the interest of justice to do so.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C § 1391(b) (setting forth the basic venue rules).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1406 (a) (establishing the rules for transferring a case when venue is improper).
questions.zh-question: 一家拥有并运营直升机的公司，在一个包括A州东区和B州西区在内的大都市区内为商务人士提供交通服务。一名乘客的遗孀，因直升机在A州东区坠毁身亡，在A州西区的联邦地区法院对该公司提起了非正常死亡诉讼（wrongful death action）。该公司在B州注册成立，其主要营业地（principal place of business）在C州。该公司未在答辩前提交驳回动议（pre-answer motion to dismiss）。在其答辩状（answer）中，该公司主张管辖地（venue）不当，并请求法院驳回该诉讼。如果法院认定为了司法公正（in the interest of justice），法院是否可以将该诉讼移送（transfer）至A州东区？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该公司未在答辩前提交驳回动议。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为如果法院认定管辖地不当，则必须驳回该诉讼。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法院可以主动将诉讼从一个适当的管辖地移送至另一个适当的管辖地。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为A州东区是适当的管辖地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 管辖与审判地

正确答案: D

法院可以根据司法公正的考量，将案件从不适当的审判地转移到适当的审判地。

核心法律规则

联邦法院的审判地规则 (Venue)

在联邦民事诉讼中，venue（审判地）通常在以下任一司法区是适当的：

  • 任何被告居住的司法区，如果所有被告都居住在同一州内。
  • 引起诉讼的事件或遗漏的实质部分发生地，或争议财产的实质部分所在地。
  • 如果上述两项都不适用，则为任何被告受法院属人管辖权 (personal jurisdiction) 约束的司法区。

对于公司而言，其“居住地”是指其受属人管辖权约束的任何司法区。这通常包括其注册地 (state of incorporation) 和主要营业地 (principal place of business)。

不适当审判地的处理 (Transfer or Dismissal from Improper Venue)

根据《美国法典》第28卷第1406条 (28 U.S.C. § 1406)，如果审判地不适当，联邦法院必须：

  1. 驳回案件 (dismiss the case)；或
  2. 如果符合司法公正的利益，将案件转移到适当的审判地 (transfer to a proper venue)。

被告可以通过在答辩状中提出或在答辩状之前提出动议来主张审判地不当的抗辩。如果未及时提出，则该抗辩可能被视为放弃 (waived)。

概念比较：审判地转移

特征 从适当审判地转移 (28 U.S.C. § 1404) 从不适当审判地转移/驳回 (28 U.S.C. § 1406)
初始审判地 适当的 (proper) 不适当的 (improper)
法院权力 可以 (may) 转移 必须 (must) 驳回或转移
转移目的地 任何其他适当的审判地，且当事人可以被管辖的司法区 任何适当的审判地
转移理由 为了当事人/证人的方便，以及司法公正的利益 为了司法公正的利益
属人管辖权 转移法院必须对被告有属人管辖权 转移法院不需要对被告有属人管辖权，只要能将案件转移到有属人管辖权的适当审判地即可

案件事实与适用逻辑

第一步：确定原告选择的审判地是否适当。

本案中，原告在州A西区联邦法院提起诉讼。我们需要根据《美国法典》第28卷第1391条 (28 U.S.C. § 1391) 来评估其适当性。

  • 被告居住地规则 (§ 1391(b)(1))：被告公司在州B注册，主要营业地在州C。因此，该公司不居住在州A西区。此规则不适用。
  • 事件发生地规则 (§ 1391(b)(2))：直升机坠毁（引起诉讼的事件）发生在州A东区，而非州A西区。此规则不适用。
  • 兜底条款 (§ 1391(b)(3))：没有迹象表明前两条规则无法确定审判地，或被告仅在州A西区受属人管辖。

结论：因此，原告选择的州A西区是一个不适当的审判地。

第二步：确定当审判地不适当时的法院权力。

由于审判地不适当，法院必须适用《美国法典》第28卷第1406条 (28 U.S.C. § 1406)。根据该条，法院可以选择驳回案件，或者在符合司法公正利益的情况下，将案件转移到适当的审判地。

第三步：确定州A东区是否是适当的审判地。

直升机坠毁事件发生在州A东区。根据《美国法典》第28卷第1391(b)(2)条，引起诉讼的事件的实质部分发生地是适当的审判地。因此，州A东区是一个适当的审判地。

第四步：评估法院是否可以转移案件。

由于州A西区审判地不适当，且州A东区是适当的审判地，法院可以根据《美国法典》第28卷第1406条，在符合司法公正利益的情况下，将案件转移到州A东区。

第五步：考虑被告是否放弃了审判地不当的抗辩。

被告在答辩状中提出了审判地不当的抗辩。根据联邦民事诉讼规则，在答辩状中提出该抗辩是及时且有效的，因此被告并未放弃此防御。

审判地转移决策流程图

案件提起
↓
审判地是否适当？
是 (Proper) ↓
适用 28 U.S.C. § 1404
↓
可为方便和公正转移到其他适当审判地
否 (Improper) ↓
适用 28 U.S.C. § 1406
↓
法院必须驳回或在公正利益下转移到适当审判地

MBE 考点陷阱提示

考生常混淆《美国法典》第1404条和第1406条。关键区别在于初始审判地是否适当。

  • § 1404 适用于适当的审判地之间的转移，通常是为了方便当事人或证人。
  • § 1406 适用于不适当的审判地，法院可以选择驳回或转移到适当的审判地，以维护司法公正。

此外，请注意审判地不当抗辩的放弃。如果被告未在答辩状中或答辩状之前提出此抗辩，则可能被视为放弃。

正确答案与干扰项排除

D. 是的，因为州A东区是适当的审判地。

解释：本案中，原告选择的州A西区并非适当的审判地，因为被告公司不居住在该区，且导致诉讼的事件也未发生在该区。根据《美国法典》第28卷第1406条，当审判地不适当，法院可以选择驳回案件或将其转移到适当的审判地，前提是符合司法公正的利益。由于直升机坠毁事件发生在州A东区，根据《美国法典》第28卷第1391(b)(2)条，州A东区是一个适当的审判地。因此，法院可以根据司法公正的考量，将案件转移到州A东区。

A. 否，因为公司未能在答辩状之前提出驳回动议。

解释：错误。被告可以在答辩状中提出审判地不当的抗辩，也可以在答辩状之前通过动议提出。本案中，公司在答辩状中提出了该抗辩，因此并未放弃此防御。

B. 否，因为如果法院认定审判地不适当，则必须驳回诉讼。

解释：错误。根据《美国法典》第28卷第1406条，当审判地不适当，法院有权选择驳回案件或将其转移到适当的审判地，如果转移符合司法公正的利益。法院并非必须驳回。

C. 是的，因为法院可以主动将案件从一个适当的审判地转移到另一个适当的审判地。

解释：错误。本案的初始审判地（州A西区）是不适当的，因此不适用《美国法典》第28卷第1404条（从适当审判地转移）。此外，即使在§ 1404下，转移通常也需要当事人提出动议，而非法院主动。本案应适用§ 1406，它处理的是从不适当审判地转移的情况。

MBE 考试技巧

遇到审判地问题时，首先判断初始审判地是否适当。如果适当，考虑《美国法典》第1404条（便利性转移）；如果不适当，考虑《美国法典》第1406条（驳回或转移到适当审判地）。同时，务必检查被告是否及时提出了审判地不当的抗辩，以避免放弃。

参考文献

28 U.S.C § 1391(b) (规定基本的审判地规则) 28 U.S.C § 1406(a) (规定审判地不当时案件转移的规则)

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Patients who took a prescription drug joined as plaintiffs in a lawsuit based on a state-law products liability claim in State A court. Two-thirds of the individuals were residents of State A. The other one-third were residents of other states. Each plaintiff acquired the drug, took it, and allegedly suffered the adverse health consequences of having done so in his or her state of residence.
The defendant, a drug manufacturer, was incorporated in State B and had its principal headquarters in State C. The defendant had significant contacts with State A, marketing and selling the drug there as well as in every state in the United States. The drug was manufactured in State C.
Does the state court in State A have specific personal jurisdiction over the manufacturer with regard to the out-of-state residents' claims?

choices.A: No, because the out-of-state residents' injuries did not arise from the manufacturer's conduct in State A.
choices.B: No, because the manufacturer was not incorporated in State A and did not have its headquarters there.
choices.C: Yes, because the out-of-state residents' injuries arose from the same allegedly defective product as the in-state residents' injuries.
choices.D: Yes, because the manufacturer marketed and sold the drug nationwide.

questions.explanation:
Personal jurisdiction
(court's authority over defendant)
Type Requirements
Service of
process		 • Serving process on defendant voluntarily in state where court is located (ie, forum state)
Consent • Express – contractual agreement (eg, forum-selection clause)
• Implied – engaging in specific activity that state has substantial interest in regulating (eg, driving on public roads)
• Waiver – untimely objection to personal jurisdiction
• Appearance – voluntarily appearing in court to litigate merits of case
Specific
(case-linked)		 • Plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to defendant's minimum contacts (ie, purposeful availment) with forum state AND
• Exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play & substantial justice
General
(all-purpose)		 • Defendant has continuous & systematic contacts with forum state so substantial that defendant is essentially "at home" (ie, defendant's domicile)

A court must have personal jurisdiction—i.e., authority over the parties (or property) before it—to hear a dispute. Personal jurisdiction can be established through specific jurisdiction, which exists when:

  • the plaintiff's claim arises from or is closely related to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and
  • the exercise of jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice (see factors listed in table above).

Here, the out-of-state residents brought claims against the manufacturer in State A (forum state). But their injuries did not arise out of, and are not closely related to, the manufacturer's contacts with State A. Instead, their injuries arose from the manufacturer's conduct in each of their own states (i.e., selling the drug there).* And because the out-of-state residents' injuries did not arise from the manufacturer's conduct in State A, the State A court does not have specific personal jurisdiction over the manufacturer with regard to the out-of-state residents' claims.

*For example, the injury of a plaintiff who resides in State D would have arisen from the manufacturer's conduct of marketing and selling the drug in State D—this claim would be completely unrelated to the manufacturer's conduct of marketing and selling the drug in State A.

(Choice B) A corporation is subject to general personal jurisdiction only where it is "at home"—i.e., in its state of incorporation and in the state of its principal place of business. But a corporation can also be subject to specific personal jurisdiction in other states if the above requirements are satisfied (not seen here).

(Choice C) Although the out-of-state residents joined as plaintiffs with the State A residents, the court must still have personal jurisdiction over the manufacturer with respect to each claim. The State A residents can likely establish specific personal jurisdiction for their own claims, but that is irrelevant to the out-of-state residents' claims.

(Choice D) Since the drug was marketed and sold nationwide, each out-of-state resident could argue that the manufacturer is subject to specific personal jurisdiction in his or her home state with respect to his or her claim. But this does not establish the necessary link between the injuries suffered by each out-of-state resident and State A.

📌 Educational Objective

Specific personal jurisdiction exists when the plaintiff's claim arises from or closely relates to the defendant's minimum contacts with the forum state and exercising jurisdiction complies with notions of fair play and substantial justice.

📚 References
  • Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (explaining the requirements for specific jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question:
服用某处方药的患者作为原告，在A州法院提起了一项基于州法律的“产品责任”（products liability）诉讼。其中三分之二的个人是A州居民，另外三分之一是其他州的居民。每位原告都在其居住州获取、服用该药物，并据称因此遭受了不良健康后果。
被告是一家制药商，在B州注册成立（incorporated），其主要总部（principal headquarters）设在C州。被告与A州有重要联系，在该州以及美国所有州销售和推广该药物。该药物在C州生产。
A州州法院对制造商是否就州外居民的索赔（claims）拥有“特定属人管辖权”（specific personal jurisdiction）？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为州外居民的伤害并非源于制造商在A州的行为。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为制造商并非在A州注册成立，且其总部也不设在该州。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为州外居民的伤害与州内居民的伤害源于同一据称有缺陷的产品。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为制造商在全国范围内销售和推广该药物。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

民事诉讼法: 管辖权与审判地

正确答案：A

判决摘要：对于非本州居民的诉讼请求，州A法院对制造商不具有特定属人管辖权，因为这些请求并非源于制造商在州A的活动。

核心法律规则

属人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction)

法院必须对当事人（或财产）具有属人管辖权（personal jurisdiction）——即，在审理纠纷之前，法院对当事人（或财产）拥有权力。属人管辖权可以通过以下方式确立：

  • 送达程序 (Service of process)：在法院所在地（即法院地州）自愿向被告送达传票。
  • 同意 (Consent)：被告明示或默示同意，或通过弃权、出庭等方式同意。
  • 特定属人管辖权 (Specific personal jurisdiction)：当原告的诉讼请求源于或与被告在法院地州的最低联系密切相关，且行使管辖权符合公平合理和实质正义的理念时。
  • 一般属人管辖权 (General personal jurisdiction)：当被告与法院地州有持续且系统的联系，以至于被告在该州基本上是“在家”（即，被告的住所地）时。

本题主要考察特定属人管辖权，其核心在于“诉讼请求源于或与被告在法院地州的最低联系密切相关”这一要求。

属人管辖权类型与要求

类型 要求
送达程序 在法院所在地（即法院地州）自愿向被告送达传票
同意
  • 明示 – 合同约定（例如，法院地选择条款）
  • 默示 – 从事特定活动（例如，在公共道路上驾驶），该州对监管此活动有实质性利益
  • 弃权 – 未及时对属人管辖权提出异议
  • 出庭 – 自愿出庭审理案件实体
特定 (与案件相关)
  • 原告的诉讼请求源于或与被告在法院地州的最低联系（即，有目的的利用）密切相关 AND
  • 行使管辖权符合公平合理和实质正义的理念
一般 (全目的) 被告与法院地州有持续且系统的联系，以至于被告在该州基本上是“在家”（即，被告的住所地）

案件事实与适用逻辑

本案中，非本州居民对州A（法院地州）的制造商提起了诉讼。但根据案件事实：

  • 非本州居民的伤害并非源于制造商在州A的活动。
  • 这些伤害也与制造商在州A的联系不密切。
  • 相反，非本州居民的伤害源于制造商在他们各自居住州的活动（即，在该州销售药品）。

因此，州A法院对制造商不具有针对非本州居民诉讼请求的特定属人管辖权。

*例如，居住在州D的原告的伤害如果源于制造商在州D的营销和销售药品行为，那么该诉讼请求将与制造商在州A的营销和销售药品行为完全无关。

制造商 (州B注册，州C总部)
↓ (全国销售药品)
州A居民
↓ (在州A购买/使用药品)
在州A受伤
↓
在州A提起诉讼 (特定属人管辖权 OK)
非本州居民
↓ (在各自州购买/使用药品)
在各自州受伤
↓
在州A提起诉讼 (特定属人管辖权 NOT OK)

图示：特定属人管辖权要求诉讼请求与法院地州的联系

易错点警示

混淆一般属人管辖权与特定属人管辖权： 仅仅因为被告在法院地州有广泛的业务活动（可能足以确立一般属人管辖权，如果该州是其“住所地”），或者与其他原告的诉讼请求有联系，并不意味着对所有原告的诉讼请求都具有特定属人管辖权。特定属人管辖权要求每个诉讼请求都必须单独评估其与法院地州联系的充分性。

“集体诉讼”的误区： 即使是集体诉讼或多方原告共同诉讼，法院也必须对每一位原告的诉讼请求单独判断是否存在属人管辖权。一个原告的有效联系不能“传染”给其他没有足够联系的原告。

正确答案与干扰项排除

A. 否，因为非本州居民的伤害并非源于制造商在州A的活动。

正确。 特定属人管辖权的核心要求是原告的诉讼请求必须“源于或与被告在法院地州的最低联系密切相关”。本案中，非本州居民的伤害是在他们各自的州内因购买和使用药品而遭受的，与制造商在州A的活动没有直接的因果联系。因此，州A法院对这些非本州居民的诉讼请求不具有特定属人管辖权。

B. 否，因为制造商未在州A注册成立，也未在此设立总部。

错误。 本选项描述的是一般属人管辖权的标准，即公司在其注册地和主要营业地被视为“在家”，因此受一般属人管辖。但本题考察的是特定属人管辖权。即使制造商不在州A注册或设立总部，如果其在州A的活动与原告的诉讼请求之间存在足够联系，仍可能确立特定属人管辖权。然而，对于非本州居民的诉讼请求，这种联系并不存在。

C. 是，因为非本州居民的伤害与本州居民的伤害源于同一据称有缺陷的产品。

错误。 尽管所有原告的伤害都源于同一产品，但特定属人管辖权要求每个原告的诉讼请求都必须与被告在法院地州有独立的联系。一个原告的有效联系不能自动延伸到其他原告。非本州居民的诉讼请求与制造商在州A的活动之间缺乏必要的联系，即使本州居民的诉讼请求可能具有特定属人管辖权。

D. 是，因为制造商在全国范围内销售该药品。

错误。 制造商在全国范围内销售药品表明其在许多州都有联系，但这并不意味着任何一个州都可以对所有因该产品引起的诉讼行使特定属人管辖权。关键在于，非本州居民的伤害必须与制造商在州A的特定活动有联系。仅仅是全国性的销售，如果没有与州A的特定联系，不足以确立州A法院对非本州居民诉讼请求的特定属人管辖权。

考试技巧

在判断特定属人管辖权时，始终要问自己两个问题：

  1. 原告的诉讼请求是否源于或与被告在法院地州的最低联系密切相关？（即，是否存在“案情关联性”）
  2. 行使管辖权是否符合公平合理和实质正义的理念？

如果第一个问题答案为“否”，则通常不存在特定属人管辖权。记住，每个原告的诉讼请求都必须单独满足这一要求，不能因为其他原告的联系而“搭便车”。

参考文献

Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 137 S. Ct. 1773, 1780–82 (2017) (解释特定属人管辖权的要求)
